documents.t: A TDC quantizes Δt\Delta tΔt into an integer number of Δtres\Delta t_{res}Δtres​ using a chain of delay elements (typically an inverter chain). As long as the phase error is "busy" enough (fractional-N, or dithered), the quantization error can be treated as white noise. Step by step: (i) Uniform quantization error. The quantization error ete_tet​ is uniformly distributed over ±Δtres/2\pm\Delta t_{res}/2±Δtres​/2: σt2=Δtres212[s2].\sigma_{t}^2=\frac{\Delta t_{res}^2}{12}\qquad[\text{s}^2].σt2​=12Δtres2​​[s2]. (The same uniform-distribution formula as σe2=Δ2/12\sigma_e^2=\Delta^2/12σe2​=Δ2/12 in the ΔΣ third term, except that Δ\DeltaΔ there is in "cycles" and here it is in "seconds".) (ii) Time error → output phase. One output period TVT_VTV​ corresponds to 2π2\pi2π rad, so ϕTDC=2π etTV⟹σϕ2=(2π)212(ΔtresTV)2[rad2].\phi_{TDC}=2\pi\,\frac{e_t}{T_V}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \sigma_\phi^2=\frac{(2\pi)^2}{12}\Big(\frac{\Delta t_{res}}{T_V}\Big)^2\qquad[\text{rad}^2].ϕTDC​=2πTV​et​​⟹σϕ2​=12(2π)2​(TV​Δtres​​)2[rad2]. This step is where the "no N2N^2N2" lives: TVT_VTV​ is the output period, so ϕTDC\phi_{TDC}ϕTDC​ is already rad of output phase. If you insist on referring it to the reference side (dividing by TR=NTVT_R=NT_VTR​=NTV​), you get ϕ/N\phi/Nϕ/N, and going back to the output requires ×N\times N×N (power ×N2\times N^2×N2) — which cancels exactly. The most common rookie budget mistake is to multiply it by N2N^2N2 once more (the same trap as step (iv) of the ΔΣ section in pll_noise_budget). (iii) Whitening at fRf_RfR​. The TDC produces one sample per reference period; the white sequence's power σϕ2\sigma_\phi^2σϕ2​ spreads uniformly over ±fR/2\pm f_R/2±fR​/2 (two-sided bookkeeping) → density σϕ2/fR\sigma_\phi^2/f_Rσϕ2​/fR​ per Hz: LTDC=(2π)212(ΔtresTV)21fR,STDC=2 LTDC=(2π)26(ΔtresTV)21fR\mathcal{L}_{TDC}=\frac{(2\pi)^2}{12}\Big(\frac{\Delta t_{res}}{T_V}\Big)^2\frac{1}{f_R},\qquad S_{TDC}=2\,\mathcal{L}_{TDC}=\frac{(2\pi)^2}{6}\Big(\frac{\Delta t_{res}}{T_V}\Big)^2\frac{1}{f_R}LTDC​=12(2π)2​(TV​Δtres​​)2fR​1​,STDC​=2LTDC​=6(2π)2​(TV​Δtres​​)2fR​1​ (STDCS_{TDC}STDC​ in rad2/Hz\text{rad}^2/\text{Hz}rad2/Hz, single-sided, referred to the output, before the loop). Factor-of-2 bookkeeping flag (flagged every time): the literature's customary 1/121/121/12 version is two-sided bookkeeping, which numerically equals the SSB L\mathcal{L}L (the 12\tfrac1221​ in L≈12Sϕ\mathcal{L}\approx\tfrac12S_\phiL≈21​Sϕ​ cancels the ×2\times2×2 of single-siding); this site's strict single-sided SϕS_\phiSϕ​ convention needs the ×2\times2×2 (giving 1/61/61/6). This is the same class of factor-of-2 issue as [P1] Eq.(21)'s /4 (SSB bookkeeping) vs the clean time-domain /2, and as the ΔΣ third term's 1/121/121/12 vs 1/61/61/6. (iv) Into the loop. It sits in the PFD's seat, shares the path of SrefN2S_{ref}N^2Sref​N2 and is low-passed by the same ∣Hlp∣2\lvert H_{lp}\rvert^2∣Hlp​∣2; for f≪fnf\ll f_nf≪fn​ it is a flat floor (white, no shaping), flat all the way to fR/2f_R/2fR​/2. So the TDC is the ADPLL's "in-band floor setter" — just as the charge-pump is for the analog PLL. Dimension check: (2π)2(2\pi)^2(2π)2 [rad²] ×(Δtres/TV)2\times(\Delta t_{res}/T_V)^2×(Δtres​/TV​)2 [s²/s² = dimensionless] ×1/fR\times1/f_R×1/fR​ [s = 1/Hz] =rad2/Hz=\text{rad}^2/\text{Hz}=rad2/Hz — checks out.

documents.t: Example 1: f0=5f_0=5f0​=5 GHz (TV=200T_V=200TV​=200 ps), fR=50f_R=50fR​=50 MHz (N=100N=100N=100, as in Example 3 of pll_noise_budget). Find LTDC\mathcal{L}_{TDC}LTDC​ for Δtres=10\Delta t_{res}=10Δtres​=10 ps and 20 ps, compare with that page's in-band floor of −121.2-121.2−121.2 dBc/Hz, and then solve for "how fine must the TDC be to break even with the charge-pump". Step-by-step substitution (10 ps): Quantization step as a fraction of the period: Δtres/TV=10/200=0.05\Delta t_{res}/T_V=10/200=0.05Δtres​/TV​=10/200=0.05; squared 2.5×10−32.5\times10^{-3}2.5×10−3 (dimensionless). Prefactor: (2π)2/12=39.478/12=3.290(2\pi)^2/12=39.478/12=3.290(2π)2/12=39.478/12=3.290 [rad²]. Phase variance: 3.290×2.5×10−3=8.225×10−3 rad23.290\times2.5\times10^{-3}=8.225\times10^{-3}\ \text{rad}^23.290×2.5×10−3=8.225×10−3 rad2 (σϕ=90.7\sigma_\phi=90.7σϕ​=90.7 mrad, i.e. σt=Δtres/12=2.887\sigma_t=\Delta t_{res}/\sqrt{12}=2.887σt​=Δtres​/12​=2.887 ps rms). Spread over fRf_RfR​: 8.225×10−3/(5×107)=1.645×10−108.225\times10^{-3}/(5\times10^7)=1.645\times10^{-10}8.225×10−3/(5×107)=1.645×10−10 → LTDC=10log⁡10(1.645×10−10)=−97.8\mathcal{L}_{TDC}=10\log_{10}(1.645\times10^{-10})=-97.8LTDC​=10log10​(1.645×10−10)=−97.8 dBc/Hz. 20 ps: (Δtres/TV)2(\Delta t_{res}/T_V)^2(Δtres​/TV​)2 is 4 times larger (+6.02+6.02+6.02 dB) → −91.8-91.8−91.8 dBc/Hz. Result and interpretation: a 10 ps TDC gives a flat in-band floor of −97.8-97.8−97.8 dBc/Hz, 23.4 dB above the analog PLL's −121.2-121.2−121.2 dBc/Hz (reference×N2\times N^2×N2 + CP). Solving backwards: for LTDC\mathcal{L}_{TDC}LTDC​ to equal 7.5×10−137.5\times10^{-13}7.5×10−13 (i.e. −121.2-121.2−121.2 dBc/Hz) requires Δtres=TV12 L fR/(2π)=0.675\Delta t_{res}=T_V\sqrt{12\,\mathcal{L}\,f_R}/(2\pi)=0.675Δtres​=TV​12LfR​​/(2π)=0.675 ps — finer than a single inverter delay in an advanced process (a few ps), unreachable with a plain inverter chain. This is the main battlefield of ADPLL literature for the past decade: (a) push Δtres\Delta t_{res}Δtres​ below a picosecond with interpolation, Vernier, or GRO (gated ring oscillator) techniques; (b) DTC assistance (digital-to-time converter: first shift the reference edge by the "predicted fractional phase", so the TDC only has to measure a tiny residual → a short, fine, linear TDC suffices); (c) simply use a bang-bang PD (1-bit TDC) — the quantization error is then no longer uniform white noise but is linearized by the input jitter (the KbbK_{bb}Kbb​ of the bang-bang CDR in this site's SerDes chapter is exactly that mechanism). All three roads share one goal: bring the (Δtres/TV)2(\Delta t_{res}/T_V)^2(Δtres​/TV​)2 term above down to the same order as SrefN2S_{ref}N^2Sref​N2. Dimension check: as above; after 10log⁡1010\log_{10}10log10​ read as dBc/Hz — checks out; the inverse formula s×[1/Hz]⋅[Hz]=s\text{s}\times\sqrt{[1/\text{Hz}]\cdot[\text{Hz}]}=\text{s}s×[1/Hz]⋅[Hz]​=s — checks out. import numpy as np f0, fR = 5e9, 50e6 T_V = 1/f0 for dt_res in (10e-12, 20e-12): L_tdc = (2*np.pi)**2/12*(dt_res/T_V)**2/fR print(round(dt_res*1e12), "ps", f"{L_tdc:.4e}", round(10*np.log10(L_tdc), 2)) # -> 10 ps 1.6449e-10 -97.84 # -> 20 ps 6.5797e-10 -91.82 sigma_t = 10e-12/np.sqrt(12); sigma_phi = 2*np.pi*sigma_t/T_V print(round(sigma_t*1e12, 3), round(sigma_phi*1e3, 2), f"{sigma_phi**2/fR:.4e}") # -> 2.887 90.69 1.6449e-10 (sigma_t ps, sigma_phi mrad, sigma_phi^2/f_R = L_TDC) L_cp = 0.5*1.5e-12 dt_eq = T_V*np.sqrt(12*L_cp*fR)/(2*np.pi) print(round(10*np.log10(L_cp), 1), round(dt_eq*1e12, 3), round(10*np.log10(1.6449e-10/L_cp), 1)) # -> -121.2 0.675 23.4 (analog in-band floor ref×N² + CP in dBc/Hz, break-even dt_res ps, excess of the 10 ps TDC in dB)

documents.t: The DCO control word is updated once per reference period, and its finest bank is Δfres\Delta f_{res}Δfres​. The frequency the loop wants lies between two steps; the DCO can only take the nearest — the frequency quantization error efe_fef​ is uniform over ±Δfres/2\pm\Delta f_{res}/2±Δfres​/2. From here we follow Step 2 of the varactor page exactly, with the entry replaced from "KVCOvnK_{VCO}v_nKVCO​vn​" by "efe_fef​": (i) Uniform frequency error. σf2=Δfres2/12\sigma_f^2=\Delta f_{res}^2/12σf2​=Δfres2​/12 [Hz²]. (ii) ZOH (zero-order hold) whitening at fRf_RfR​. The control word is constant within a reference period (held for TR=1/fRT_R=1/f_RTR​=1/fR​), so ef(t)e_f(t)ef​(t) is "a white sequence at rate fRf_RfR​ through a ZOH": the power σf2\sigma_f^2σf2​ spread over ±fR/2\pm f_R/2±fR​/2 (two-sided) gives density σf2/fR\sigma_f^2/f_Rσf2​/fR​, and the ZOH's squared magnitude response is sinc2(f/fR)\mathrm{sinc}^2(f/f_R)sinc2(f/fR​) (sinc(x)=sin⁡(πx)/(πx)\mathrm{sinc}(x)=\sin(\pi x)/(\pi x)sinc(x)=sin(πx)/(πx)): SΔf(f)=Δfres212 1fR sinc2(ffR)[Hz2/Hz].S_{\Delta f}(f)=\frac{\Delta f_{res}^2}{12}\,\frac{1}{f_R}\,\mathrm{sinc}^2\Big(\frac{f}{f_R}\Big)\qquad[\text{Hz}^2/\text{Hz}].SΔf​(f)=12Δfres2​​fR​1​sinc2(fR​f​)[Hz2/Hz]. (iii) Frequency → phase: the same integrator. ϕ(t)=2π∫tef dt′\phi(t)=2\pi\int^t e_f\,dt'ϕ(t)=2π∫tef​dt′; in the power domain multiply by (2π)2/Δω2=1/Δf2(2\pi)^2/\Delta\omega^2=1/\Delta f^2(2π)2/Δω2=1/Δf2 (varactor page Step 2.3, the 2π2\pi2π cancels top and bottom): LDCO(Δf)=112(ΔfresΔf)21fR sinc2(ΔffR),SDCO=2 LDCO\mathcal{L}_{DCO}(\Delta f)=\frac{1}{12}\Big(\frac{\Delta f_{res}}{\Delta f}\Big)^2\frac{1}{f_R}\,\mathrm{sinc}^2\Big(\frac{\Delta f}{f_R}\Big),\qquad S_{DCO}=2\,\mathcal{L}_{DCO}LDCO​(Δf)=121​(ΔfΔfres​​)2fR​1​sinc2(fR​Δf​),SDCO​=2LDCO​ (same factor-of-2 flag: 1/121/121/12 is the two-sided reading = the SSB number; this site's single-sided SϕS_\phiSϕ​ needs ×2\times2×2.) (iv) Into the loop. It sits in the VCO's seat and is high-passed by ∣Hhp∣2\lvert H_{hp}\rvert^2∣Hhp​∣2 — inside fnf_nfn​ the loop corrects it away (just as it corrects the VCO's close-in drift), outside fnf_nfn​ it leaks out unchanged. Shape: for Δf≪fR\Delta f\ll f_RΔf≪fR​, sinc2≈1\mathrm{sinc}^2\approx1sinc2≈1 and LDCO∝1/Δf2\mathcal{L}_{DCO}\propto1/\Delta f^2LDCO​∝1/Δf2 — 20 dB down per decade, the same slope as the VCO's white-noise 1/f21/f^21/f2 skirt; near fR/2f_R/2fR​/2 the sinc2\mathrm{sinc}^2sinc2 pushes it down a bit further. Dimension check: (Δfres/Δf)2(\Delta f_{res}/\Delta f)^2(Δfres​/Δf)2 [Hz²/Hz² = dimensionless] ×1/fR\times1/f_R×1/fR​ [1/Hz] ×sinc2\times\mathrm{sinc}^2×sinc2 [dimensionless] =1/Hz=1/\text{Hz}=1/Hz; phase is dimensionless (rad), so read as rad2/Hz\text{rad}^2/\text{Hz}rad2/Hz — checks out (the same unit argument as the varactor page's KVCO2Sv/Δf2K_{VCO}^2S_v/\Delta f^2KVCO2​Sv​/Δf2). Division of labour with the ISF (the same sentence as the varactor page): Γ\GammaΓ handles "a current impulse Δq\Delta qΔq hitting the tank at a given phase → how much phase"; Δfres\Delta f_{res}Δfres​ handles "a quasi-static frequency step → how much phase after integration". Both roads converge on the same 1/Δω21/\Delta\omega^21/Δω2 integrator — that is what "the same bookkeeping" in this page's title means. The ISF has two further appearances inside a DCO: the DCO's own device noise SvcoS_{vco}Svco​ (Γrms2/qmax2\Gamma_{rms}^2/q_{max}^2Γrms2​/qmax2​, completely unchanged); and the charge kickback Δq\Delta qΔq injected into the tank when a unit capacitor switches — the phase at which it lands (Γ(ω0τ)\Gamma(\omega_0\tau)Γ(ω0​τ)) decides how much phase jump and spur the dither causes ([P1] operational definition Δϕ=ΓΔq/qmax\Delta\phi=\Gamma\Delta q/q_{max}Δϕ=ΓΔq/qmax​).

documents.t: Example 2: f0=5f_0=5f0​=5 GHz, fR=50f_R=50fR​=50 MHz, Δfres=10\Delta f_{res}=10Δfres​=10 kHz (2 ppm). Find LDCO\mathcal{L}_{DCO}LDCO​ at Δf=0.1\Delta f=0.1Δf=0.1, 1, 10 MHz; convert to the ΔC\Delta CΔC of the finest unit capacitor (tank C=1C=1C=1 pF). Step-by-step substitution (1 MHz): (Δfres/Δf)2=(104/106)2=10−4(\Delta f_{res}/\Delta f)^2=(10^4/10^6)^2=10^{-4}(Δfres​/Δf)2=(104/106)2=10−4 (dimensionless). ×1/12=8.333×10−6\times1/12=8.333\times10^{-6}×1/12=8.333×10−6; ×1/fR=8.333×10−6/(5×107)=1.667×10−13\times1/f_R=8.333\times10^{-6}/(5\times10^7)=1.667\times10^{-13}×1/fR​=8.333×10−6/(5×107)=1.667×10−13. ZOH: sinc2(106/5×107)=sinc2(0.02)=0.9987\mathrm{sinc}^2(10^6/5\times10^7)=\mathrm{sinc}^2(0.02)=0.9987sinc2(106/5×107)=sinc2(0.02)=0.9987 (−0.006-0.006−0.006 dB, negligible). LDCO(1 MHz)=10log⁡10(1.665×10−13)=−127.8\mathcal{L}_{DCO}(1\text{ MHz})=10\log_{10}(1.665\times10^{-13})=-127.8LDCO​(1 MHz)=10log10​(1.665×10−13)=−127.8 dBc/Hz. 0.1 MHz: ×100\times100×100 → −107.8-107.8−107.8; 10 MHz: ×1/100\times1/100×1/100 times sinc2(0.2)=0.875\mathrm{sinc}^2(0.2)=0.875sinc2(0.2)=0.875 (−0.58-0.58−0.58 dB) → −148.4-148.4−148.4 dBc/Hz. −20-20−20 dB per decade (plus the sinc extra as Δf→fR/2\Delta f\to f_R/2Δf→fR​/2). Unit capacitor: f0∝1/LCf_0\propto1/\sqrt{LC}f0​∝1/LC​ → Δf0/f0=−12ΔC/C\Delta f_0/f_0=-\tfrac12\Delta C/CΔf0​/f0​=−21​ΔC/C → ΔC=2C Δfres/f0=2×10−12×104/(5×109)=4.0\Delta C=2C\,\Delta f_{res}/f_0=2\times10^{-12}\times10^4/(5\times10^9)=4.0ΔC=2CΔfres​/f0​=2×10−12×104/(5×109)=4.0 aF. Result and interpretation: −127.8-127.8−127.8 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz is 27.8 dB below the lab_20 ring VCO's −100-100−100 dBc/Hz — a ring-DCO does not care at all; but it is 20 dB above the site's canonical LC value of −148-148−148 dBc/Hz (Example B): a good LC-DCO would be drowned by its own quantization noise. And a 4 aF unit capacitor cannot be built physically (parasitics alone are two orders of magnitude larger) — so a DCO must be ΔΣ-dithered (Step 4): a buildable, coarser unit cell (tens of aF to fF) is toggled at a fast clock to buy fine "average" resolution. Dimension check: ΔC=[F]×[Hz]/[Hz]=F\Delta C=[\text{F}]\times[\text{Hz}]/[\text{Hz}]=\text{F}ΔC=[F]×[Hz]/[Hz]=F — checks out. import numpy as np f0, fR, df_res, C = 5e9, 50e6, 10e3, 1e-12 for df in (1e5, 1e6, 1e7): L_dco = (1/12)*(df_res/df)**2/fR*np.sinc(df/fR)**2 print(round(df/1e6, 1), f"{L_dco:.4e}", round(10*np.log10(L_dco), 2), round(10*np.log10(np.sinc(df/fR)**2), 2)) # -> 0.1 1.6666e-11 -107.78 -0.0 # -> 1.0 1.6645e-13 -127.79 -0.01 # -> 10.0 1.4586e-15 -148.36 -0.58 (MHz, linear, dBc/Hz, sinc^2 correction dB) print(f"{2*C*df_res/f0*1e18:.1f}") # -> 4.0 (finest unit capacitor, aF)

documents.t: Recipe: take a dither clock fdthf_{dth}fdth​ much faster than fRf_RfR​ (usually derived by dividing CKV, e.g. f0/8f_0/8f0​/8), and use an mmm-th-order ΔΣ modulator to turn the "desired fractional frequency" into a 0/1 sequence for the finest unit cell. The algebra is exactly that of the ΔΣ third term in pll_noise_budget, except that what is shaped is frequency and the sampling rate is fdthf_{dth}fdth​: ef → (1−z−1)mef⟹SΔf(f)=Δfres212 1fdth[2sin⁡(πffdth)]2msinc2(ffdth),e_f\ \to\ (1-z^{-1})^m e_f\quad\Longrightarrow\quad S_{\Delta f}(f)=\frac{\Delta f_{res}^2}{12}\,\frac{1}{f_{dth}}\Big[2\sin\Big(\frac{\pi f}{f_{dth}}\Big)\Big]^{2m}\mathrm{sinc}^2\Big(\frac{f}{f_{dth}}\Big),ef​ → (1−z−1)mef​⟹SΔf​(f)=12Δfres2​​fdth​1​[2sin(fdth​πf​)]2msinc2(fdth​f​), then through the 1/Δf21/\Delta f^21/Δf2 integrator of Step 3: LDCO,ΔΣ(Δf)=112(ΔfresΔf)21fdth[2sin⁡(πΔffdth)]2msinc2(Δffdth).\mathcal{L}_{DCO,\Delta\Sigma}(\Delta f)=\frac{1}{12}\Big(\frac{\Delta f_{res}}{\Delta f}\Big)^2\frac{1}{f_{dth}}\Big[2\sin\Big(\frac{\pi\Delta f}{f_{dth}}\Big)\Big]^{2m}\mathrm{sinc}^2\Big(\frac{\Delta f}{f_{dth}}\Big).LDCO,ΔΣ​(Δf)=121​(ΔfΔfres​​)2fdth​1​[2sin(fdth​πΔf​)]2msinc2(fdth​Δf​). Three effects stacked together (for Δf≪fdth\Delta f\ll f_{dth}Δf≪fdth​, 2sin⁡(πΔf/fdth)≈2πΔf/fdth2\sin(\pi\Delta f/f_{dth})\approx2\pi\Delta f/f_{dth}2sin(πΔf/fdth​)≈2πΔf/fdth​): m=0m=0m=0 (just toggle faster, no shaping): the power Δfres2/12\Delta f_{res}^2/12Δfres2​/12 is spread over the wider ±fdth/2\pm f_{dth}/2±fdth​/2, gaining 10log⁡10(fdth/fR)10\log_{10}(f_{dth}/f_R)10log10​(fdth​/fR​). m=1m=1m=1: the +20+20+20 dB/dec shaping exactly cancels the integrator's −20-20−20 dB/dec → L\mathcal{L}L becomes flat in-band, with magnitude ∝(Δfres/fdth)2/fdth\propto(\Delta f_{res}/f_{dth})^2/f_{dth}∝(Δfres​/fdth​)2/fdth​, far below the unshaped version. m=2m=2m=2: a net +20+20+20 dB/dec climb — lower at low frequency, and at high frequency rely on ∣Hhp∣2\lvert H_{hp}\rvert^2∣Hhp​∣2? No: DCO noise enters the output high-passed, so the loop does not cut it at high frequency; the high-frequency hump of higher-order shaping leaks out unchanged and can only be tamed by the sinc and by downstream filtering. This is the key difference between DCO dither and fractional-N divider dither — the latter is a low-pass path where the loop cuts the high end; the former is a high-pass path where the loop does not. Hence the DCO side usually uses only first or second order and pushes fdthf_{dth}fdth​ high. Dimension check: as in Step 3; the extra [2sin⁡(⋅)]2m[2\sin(\cdot)]^{2m}[2sin(⋅)]2m is dimensionless — checks out.

documents.t: Example 3: continuing Example 2, fdth=f0/8=625f_{dth}=f_0/8=625fdth​=f0​/8=625 MHz; find LDCO,ΔΣ\mathcal{L}_{DCO,\Delta\Sigma}LDCO,ΔΣ​ at Δf=1\Delta f=1Δf=1 MHz for m=0,1,2m=0,1,2m=0,1,2. Step-by-step substitution: Spreading: fdth/fR=12.5f_{dth}/f_R=12.5fdth​/fR​=12.5 → +10.97+10.97+10.97 dB; m=0m=0m=0: −127.8−10.97=−138.8-127.8-10.97=-138.8−127.8−10.97=−138.8 dBc/Hz. Shaping factor: 2sin⁡(π×106/6.25×108)=2sin⁡(5.027×10−3)=1.0053×10−22\sin(\pi\times10^6/6.25\times10^8)=2\sin(5.027\times10^{-3})=1.0053\times10^{-2}2sin(π×106/6.25×108)=2sin(5.027×10−3)=1.0053×10−2; squared 1.011×10−41.011\times10^{-4}1.011×10−4 (−40.0-40.0−40.0 dB) → m=1m=1m=1: −178.7-178.7−178.7 dBc/Hz. m=2m=2m=2: another −40-40−40 dB → −218.7-218.7−218.7 dBc/Hz (already far below any physical floor; in practice covered by the DCO's device noise, the dither clock's own jitter and kickback spurs — the formula only accounts for the "quantization" share). Result and interpretation: first-order dither alone takes −127.8-127.8−127.8 down to −178.7-178.7−178.7 dBc/Hz (−50.9-50.9−50.9 dB), and the LC-DCO's −148-148−148 is once again the main actor. The price: the unit cell switches every 1.6 ns, and each switching event is a Δq\Delta qΔq hitting the tank — the ISF says the phase at which it lands decides how much the phase jumps (Δϕ=Γ(ω0τ)Δq/qmax\Delta\phi=\Gamma(\omega_0\tau)\Delta q/q_{max}Δϕ=Γ(ω0​τ)Δq/qmax​); when fdthf_{dth}fdth​ is synchronous with f0f_0f0​ these jumps repeat at fixed phases, one of the sources of spurs. import numpy as np f0, df_res, df = 5e9, 10e3, 1e6 f_dth = f0/8 for m in (0, 1, 2): L = (1/12)*(df_res/df)**2/f_dth*(2*np.sin(np.pi*df/f_dth))**(2*m)*np.sinc(df/f_dth)**2 print(m, f"{L:.4e}", round(10*np.log10(L), 1)) # -> 0 1.3333e-14 -138.8 # -> 1 1.3475e-18 -178.7 # -> 2 1.3618e-22 -218.7 (m, linear, dBc/Hz at 1 MHz) print(round(f_dth/1e6, 1), round(10*np.log10(f_dth/50e6), 2)) # -> 625.0 10.97 (f_dth MHz, spreading bonus dB)

The fractional-N ΔΣ third term does not exist in an ADPLL — the fractional frequency is handled directly by the fractional accumulation of RRR_RRR​, with no divider dithering; but TDC nonlinearity turns the periodic pattern of the fractional part of RRR_RRR​ into fractional spurs (see applicability and failure). ∣Hlp∣2,∣Hhp∣2\lvert H_{lp}\rvert^2,\lvert H_{hp}\rvert^2∣Hlp​∣2,∣Hhp​∣2 are the type-II second-order closed loop of spec §10.2 (the digital loop filter's zzz-domain implementation agrees with its continuous-time approximation for f≪fRf\ll f_Rf≪fR​). Step by step (spot, 10 ps): In-band term: SrefN2=10−12S_{ref}N^2=10^{-12}Sref​N2=10−12, STDC=2×1.645×10−10=3.29×10−10S_{TDC}=2\times1.645\times10^{-10}=3.29\times10^{-10}STDC​=2×1.645×10−10=3.29×10−10 (single-sided); ∣Hlp(1 MHz)∣2=1.50\lvert H_{lp}(1\text{ MHz})\rvert^2=1.50∣Hlp​(1 MHz)∣2=1.50 (peaking) → 4.95×10−104.95\times10^{-10}4.95×10−10. Total 5.95×10−105.95\times10^{-10}5.95×10−10 → L=10log⁡10(12×5.95×10−10)=−95.3\mathcal{L}=10\log_{10}(\tfrac12\times5.95\times10^{-10})=-95.3L=10log10​(21​×5.95×10−10)=−95.3 dBc/Hz. The TDC term alone is 83% — it even buries the ring VCO. 1 ps: STDCS_{TDC}STDC​ drops 100× → in-band 6.4×10−126.4\times10^{-12}6.4×10−12, the total is VCO-dominated → −102.7-102.7−102.7 dBc/Hz. Result (integrated jitter): Architecture fnf_nfn​ σt\sigma_tσt​ Reading Analog CP-PLL (Scp=5×10−13S_{cp}=5\times10^{-13}Scp​=5×10−13) 6.9 MHz 259 fs pll_noise_budget optimum ADPLL, Δtres=10\Delta t_{res}=10Δtres​=10 ps 6.9 MHz 2773 fs the TDC floor is fully passed by the wide BW ADPLL, Δtres=10\Delta t_{res}=10Δtres​=10 ps 0.47 MHz (its own optimum) 1001 fs can only narrow the BW, then the VCO leaks: 3.9×3.9\times3.9× the analog value ADPLL, Δtres=1\Delta t_{res}=1Δtres​=1 ps 6.9 MHz 363 fs close to the analog value ADPLL, Δtres=1\Delta t_{res}=1Δtres​=1 ps 3.84 MHz (its own optimum) 338 fs optimum BW slightly narrower (TDC floor still 3.4 dB above the analog in-band floor of −121.2-121.2−121.2) Interpretation: this is the numerical version of "why an ADPLL needs a fine TDC / DTC assistance / BB-PD". A 10 ps TDC pushes the optimum jitter from 259 fs to 1 ps and forces you to narrow the BW by 15× — a disaster for a noisy ring-DCO; only a 1 ps TDC returns to the same order of magnitude. Conversely, the (undithered) SDCOS_{DCO}SDCO​ is invisible in this ring toy (28 dB lower); it only surfaces with an LC-DCO, and that is when the dither of Step 4 is needed. Dimension check: ∫Sout df\int S_{out}\,df∫Sout​df [rad²] → σϕ/(2πf0)\sigma_\phi/(2\pi f_0)σϕ​/(2πf0​): rad/(rad/s) = s — checks out. import numpy as np from simulations.common.pll_utils import H_lowpass_mag2, H_highpass_mag2 f0, fR, N = 5e9, 50e6, 100 T_V = 1/f0 f = np.logspace(3, 9, 3000) S_ref = 1e-16 + 1e-18*(1e6/f) # same table as pll_noise_budget S_vco = 2e-10*(1e6/f)**2 # ring toy, L(1 MHz) = -100 dBc/Hz S_dco = 2*(1/12)*(1e4/f)**2/fR*np.sinc(f/fR)**2 # single-sided = 2 L_DCO def S_tdc(dt_res): return 2*(2*np.pi)**2/12*(dt_res/T_V)**2/fR # single-sided = 2 L_TDC def sigma_t(S_out): return np.sqrt(np.trapezoid(S_out, f))/(2*np.pi*f0) fn = 1e6 lp1, hp1 = H_lowpass_mag2(np.array([1e6]), fn)[0], H_highpass_mag2(np.array([1e6]), fn)[0] for dt in (10e-12, 1e-12): inb = (1e-12 + S_tdc(dt))*lp1 outb = (S_dco[np.argmin(abs(f-1e6))] + 2e-10)*hp1 print(round(dt*1e12), f"{inb:.3e}", f"{outb:.3e}", round(10*np.log10(0.5*(inb + outb)), 1)) # -> 10 4.950e-10 1.002e-10 -95.3 # -> 1 6.435e-12 1.002e-10 -102.7 (dt_res ps, in-band, out-of-band rad^2/Hz, L dBc/Hz) fn = 6.9e6 lp, hp = H_lowpass_mag2(f, fn), H_highpass_mag2(f, fn) print(round(sigma_t((S_ref*N**2 + 5e-13)*lp + S_vco*hp)*1e15)) # -> 259 (analog CP-PLL, fs) for dt in (10e-12, 1e-12): print(round(dt*1e12), round(sigma_t((S_ref*N**2 + S_tdc(dt))*lp + (S_dco + S_vco)*hp)*1e15)) # -> 10 2773 # -> 1 363 (ADPLL at f_n = 6.9 MHz, fs) fns = np.logspace(4.5, 7.5, 60) for dt in (10e-12, 1e-12): jit = [sigma_t((S_ref*N**2 + S_tdc(dt))*H_lowpass_mag2(f, x) + (S_dco + S_vco)*H_highpass_mag2(f, x)) for x in fns] k = int(np.argmin(jit)) print(round(dt*1e12), round(fns[k]/1e6, 2), round(jit[k]*1e15)) # -> 10 0.47 1001 # -> 1 3.84 338 (ADPLL's own optimum f_n MHz, sigma_t fs)

documents.t: The ADPLL's output σt\sigma_tσt​ (Example 4) feeds the eye diagram and BER of serdes_clocking_connection exactly as an analog PLL's does. Two ADPLL-specific reminders: (1) the TDC floor is flat white noise all the way to fR/2f_R/2fR​/2, so under a wide BW its contribution to integrated jitter grows linearly ∝fn\propto f_n∝fn​ (less "afraid" of narrowing the BW than a 1/f21/f^21/f2 source, more afraid of widening it); (2) the latency of the digital loop (TDC conversion and digital filtering each take a few reference periods) reduces phase margin and raises peaking — the "cascaded 0.1 dB" rule of pll_noise_budget must include latency in an ADPLL (external literature, beyond this page). The bang-bang CDR in a SerDes is in fact an ADPLL with a "1-bit TDC": the BB-PD linearized gain KbbK_{bb}Kbb​ mentioned in Example 1 is that road.

documents.t: Condition When it holds When it fails TDC quantization error white and uniform phase error "busy" (fractional, or dithered) → the flat floor above integer-N and locked: the TDC input barely changes → the error is a constant / short-period pattern, not white (dead-zone-like behaviour, limit cycle); dither must be injected TDC linear (small DNL/INL) only the quantization share nonlinearity turns the periodic pattern of the fractional part of RRR_RRR​ into fractional spurs and folds high-frequency noise in-band TDC dynamic range ≥TV\ge T_V≥TV​ one TDC stage suffices (TV/Δtres=20T_V/\Delta t_{res}=20TV​/Δtres​=20 cells at 10 ps) insufficient range → a DTC pre-shifts the reference edge, or coarse/fine two-stage TDC DCO quantization error white control word "busy" (dithered or fractional) a static control word → neither noise nor averaging: the frequency parks on one step (static frequency error ≤Δfres/2\le\Delta f_{res}/2≤Δfres​/2 absorbed by the loop integrator) Dither is a high-pass path m≤2m\le2m≤2, high fdthf_{dth}fdth​ → the high-frequency hump is held down by the sinc high mmm or low fdthf_{dth}fdth​ → the hump leaks out unchanged (the loop does not cut it); the dither clock's jitter and kickback spurs are separate Linear small-signal loop, fn≪fRf_n\ll f_Rfn​≪fR​ the type-II continuous-time ∣H∣2\lvert H\rvert^2∣H∣2 approximation holds fnf_nfn​ approaching fR/10f_R/10fR​/10 or above, or large digital latency → zzz-domain analysis, higher peaking Illustrative numbers structural conclusions (TDC sets in-band, DCO follows 1/f21/f^21/f2, no N2N^2N2) are trustworthy absolute dB values must not be benchmarked against any real process or published measurement

documents.t: An ADPLL replaces PFD/CP with a TDC and the VCO with a DCO; phase is counted in VCO cycles, ϕE=RR−RV−ε\phi_E=R_R-R_V-\varepsilonϕE​=RR​−RV​−ε. TDC quantization = in-band white floor (PFD seat, low-pass, no N2N^2N2): LTDC=(2π)212(ΔtresTV)21fR\mathcal{L}_{TDC}=\dfrac{(2\pi)^2}{12}\Big(\dfrac{\Delta t_{res}}{T_V}\Big)^2\dfrac{1}{f_R}LTDC​=12(2π)2​(TV​Δtres​​)2fR​1​ (two-sided reading = SSB number; this site's single-sided SϕS_\phiSϕ​ needs ×2\times2×2). f0=5f_0=5f0​=5 GHz, fR=50f_R=50fR​=50 MHz: 10 ps → −97.8-97.8−97.8, 20 ps → −91.8-91.8−91.8 dBc/Hz; breaking even with the analog in-band floor of −121.2-121.2−121.2 (ref×N² + CP) needs 0.6750.6750.675 ps. DCO quantization = white frequency noise through a ZOH → integrate → 1/Δf21/\Delta f^21/Δf2 skirt (VCO seat, high-pass): LDCO=112(ΔfresΔf)21fRsinc2(ΔffR)\mathcal{L}_{DCO}=\dfrac{1}{12}\Big(\dfrac{\Delta f_{res}}{\Delta f}\Big)^2\dfrac{1}{f_R}\mathrm{sinc}^2\Big(\dfrac{\Delta f}{f_R}\Big)LDCO​=121​(ΔfΔfres​​)2fR​1​sinc2(fR​Δf​); 10 kHz at 1 MHz → −127.8-127.8−127.8 dBc/Hz, −20-20−20 dB per decade; corresponds to ΔC=4\Delta C=4ΔC=4 aF (unbuildable → dither). ΔΣ dither: the same (1−z−1)m(1-z^{-1})^m(1−z−1)m with the sampling rate swapped for fdthf_{dth}fdth​; m=1m=1m=1 lets the +20+20+20 shaping cancel the −20-20−20 integration → flat in-band; example: f0/8f_0/8f0​/8, m=1m=1m=1 → −178.7-178.7−178.7 dBc/Hz (−50.9-50.9−50.9 dB). The DCO path is high-pass, the loop does not cut the high-frequency hump — the key difference from fractional-N divider dither. Budget: Sout=(SrefN2+STDC)∣Hlp∣2+(SDCO+Svco)∣Hhp∣2S_{out}=(S_{ref}N^2+S_{TDC})\lvert H_{lp}\rvert^2+(S_{DCO}+S_{vco})\lvert H_{hp}\rvert^2Sout​=(Sref​N2+STDC​)∣Hlp​∣2+(SDCO​+Svco​)∣Hhp​∣2; Example 4: a 10 ps TDC pushes the optimum σt\sigma_tσt​ from 259 fs to 1001 fs and narrows the BW to 0.47 MHz; only 1 ps returns to 338 fs — the raison d'être of fine TDCs / DTC assistance / BB-PDs. The ISF term (Svco∝Γrms2/qmax2S_{vco}\propto\Gamma_{rms}^2/q_{max}^2Svco​∝Γrms2​/qmax2​) is unchanged, word for word, inside a DCO; the ISF additionally decides how much spur the dither switching kickback Δq\Delta qΔq causes depending on the phase at which it lands. Every time you write 1/121/121/12, flag it: that is two-sided bookkeeping = the SSB number; this site's single-sided SϕS_\phiSϕ​ is 1/61/61/6.

documents.t: Prerequisites: serdes_clocking_connection (the loop high-pass intuition of §6, UI/eye/BER), pll_noise_budget (∣Hlp∣2,∣Hhp∣2\lvert H_{lp}\rvert^2,\lvert H_{hp}\rvert^2∣Hlp​∣2,∣Hhp​∣2, the jitter-transfer vs jitter-tolerance distinction and the JTOL worked example — reused directly here), dj_dual_dirac (Q−1(10−12)=7.03Q^{-1}(10^{-12})=7.03Q−1(10−12)=7.03, TJ@BER) | Next: exercises, lab_13_pll_cdr_transfer serdes_clocking_connection drew the CDR (clock and data recovery) as a black box that "high-passes VCO noise and low-passes input jitter." A real SerDes receiver is almost never that linear PLL: it is a bang-bang (binary, "early/late" only) digital loop whose phase detector (PD) emits only ±1\pm1±1 and whose clock phase is moved by a phase interpolator (PI) in discrete steps of UI/2b\text{UI}/2^bUI/2b. This page answers three questions designers meet daily that none of the earlier pages answered: A bang-bang PD has no "gain" — so what sets the loop bandwidth? The answer: the rms value of the jitter, which is exactly the σt\sigma_tσt​ this site has been computing all along. Here the ISF sets not only the noise but the loop dynamics. Where does the datasheet jitter-tolerance mask (JTOL) — that broken line of "−40-40−40 dB/dec at low frequency, −20-20−20 dB/dec in the middle, a plateau at high frequency" — come from? SSC (spread-spectrum clocking) is a huge, deterministic low-frequency phase excursion the CDR must track: how large, and why a first-order loop cannot follow it. Physical intuition (conclusion first): a bang-bang PD is a comparator; the slope of sign(Δt)\text{sign}(\Delta t)sign(Δt) versus Δt\Delta tΔt is infinite at 0 — but with noise present, the expected output E[sign(Δt+n)]E[\text{sign}(\Delta t+n)]E[sign(Δt+n)] is "smeared" into an error function whose slope is the finite 2/π/σj\sqrt{2/\pi}/\sigma_j2/π​/σj​. More noise, less gain, slower loop: this is a loop whose bandwidth scales itself with the jitter. JTOL is "how much eye margin is left" divided by "the fraction the loop fails to track, ∣1−H∣\lvert1-H\rvert∣1−H∣"; the triangular FM of SSC integrates to a parabolic phase of several hundred UI, and only a type-II loop with a frequency integrator can track it down to a few tenths of a UI.

documents.t: The Alexander PD (external literature, not among this site's five PDFs: J. D. H. Alexander, Electron. Lett., vol. 11, no. 22, pp. 541–542, Oct. 1975) decides whether the clock is early or late relative to the data edge from three samples: the two bit-center samples Dk−1,DkD_{k-1}, D_kDk−1​,Dk​ and, between them, the sample EkE_kEk​ aligned with the data edge. If Ek=Dk−1≠DkE_k=D_{k-1}\ne D_kEk​=Dk−1​=Dk​, the edge sample "looks like the previous bit" → the clock is late; if Ek=Dk≠Dk−1E_k=D_k\ne D_{k-1}Ek​=Dk​=Dk−1​ → the clock is early; Dk−1=DkD_{k-1}=D_kDk−1​=Dk​ (no edge) → no output. In terms of the timing error Δt\Delta tΔt of the clock edge relative to the data edge (clock early positive): ek={sign(Δtk),data transition present0,no transitione_k=\begin{cases}\text{sign}(\Delta t_k), & \text{data transition present}\\ 0, & \text{no transition}\end{cases}ek​={sign(Δtk​),0,​data transition presentno transition​ Three key points: The output is only ±1\pm1±1 (and 0): there is no information about "how large" the error is, only its direction. So it has no PD gain KPDK_{PD}KPD​ in the conventional sense (V/rad or 1/s) — exactly what Step 2 resolves. Updates only on transitions: random NRZ data has transition density ρT≈0.5\rho_T\approx0.5ρT​≈0.5; during long runs of 0s or 1s the loop is "blind," one reason specifications require 8b/10b, 64b/66b or scrambling to bound the run length. It is simultaneously the data sampler: DkD_kDk​ is the recovered data. So the CDR's lock target "clock aligned to the data edge" automatically equals "data sample at the eye center" — connecting directly to the JTOL margin UI−TJeye\text{UI}-\text{TJ}_{eye}UI−TJeye​ of Step 4.

documents.t: Setup: the real Δt\Delta tΔt is not a constant but "nominal error Δt\Delta tΔt plus a zero-mean Gaussian term nnn," n∼N(0,σj2)n\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma_j^2)n∼N(0,σj2​). This σj\sigma_jσj​ is the total rms jitter between the data edge and the sampling clock: the input data's RJ and the recovered clock's own jitter (the loop-shaped VCO σt\sigma_tσt​, the hunting of Step 3) are all included. The PD's expected output is: ⟨e⟩(Δt)=E[sign(Δt+n)]=P(n>−Δt)−P(n<−Δt)=2Φ ⁣(Δtσj)−1=erf⁡ ⁣(Δt2 σj),Φ(x)=12[1+erf⁡(x/2)].\begin{aligned} \langle e\rangle(\Delta t)&=E\big[\text{sign}(\Delta t+n)\big]=P(n>-\Delta t)-P(n<-\Delta t) =2\Phi\!\left(\frac{\Delta t}{\sigma_j}\right)-1 \\[4pt] &=\operatorname{erf}\!\left(\frac{\Delta t}{\sqrt2\,\sigma_j}\right), \qquad \Phi(x)=\tfrac12\Big[1+\operatorname{erf}\big(x/\sqrt2\big)\Big]. \end{aligned}⟨e⟩(Δt)​=E[sign(Δt+n)]=P(n>−Δt)−P(n<−Δt)=2Φ(σj​Δt​)−1=erf(2​σj​Δt​),Φ(x)=21​[1+erf(x/2​)].​ Step by step: (i) the expectation of sign is (+1)⋅P(positive)+(−1)⋅P(negative)(+1)\cdot P(\text{positive})+(-1)\cdot P(\text{negative})(+1)⋅P(positive)+(−1)⋅P(negative); (ii) the probability of n>−Δtn>-\Delta tn>−Δt is the Gaussian CDF Φ(Δt/σj)\Phi(\Delta t/\sigma_j)Φ(Δt/σj​); (iii) rewrite with the standard relation between Φ\PhiΦ and erf. The linearized gain is the slope of this curve at Δt=0\Delta t=0Δt=0: Kbb≡∂⟨e⟩∂Δt∣Δt=0=2π⋅12 σj=2π 1σj \boxed{\ K_{bb}\equiv\frac{\partial\langle e\rangle}{\partial\Delta t}\bigg|_{\Delta t=0} =\frac{2}{\sqrt\pi}\cdot\frac{1}{\sqrt2\,\sigma_j}=\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}\,\frac{1}{\sigma_j}\ } Kbb​≡∂Δt∂⟨e⟩​​Δt=0​=π​2​⋅2​σj​1​=π2​​σj​1​ ​ (Using ddxerf⁡(x)=2πe−x2\frac{d}{dx}\operatorname{erf}(x)=\frac{2}{\sqrt\pi}e^{-x^2}dxd​erf(x)=π​2​e−x2, which equals 2/π2/\sqrt\pi2/π​ at x=0x=0x=0, times the inner derivative 1/(2σj)1/(\sqrt2\sigma_j)1/(2​σj​).) Dimension check: ⟨e⟩\langle e\rangle⟨e⟩ is dimensionless, Δt\Delta tΔt is in seconds → KbbK_{bb}Kbb​ has units s−1\text{s}^{-1}s−1 ✓. Multiplying by UI gives the dimensionless gain Kbb⋅UIK_{bb}\cdot\text{UI}Kbb​⋅UI ("output per UI of error"). Physical meaning: the larger σj\sigma_jσj​, the flatter the erf and the smaller the gain. The gain of a bang-bang loop is the reciprocal of the jitter — the central result of Lee–Kundert–Razavi (external literature, not among this site's five PDFs: J. Lee, K. S. Kundert, and B. Razavi, "Analysis and Modeling of Bang-Bang Clock and Data Recovery Circuits," IEEE J. Solid-State Circuits, vol. 39, no. 9, pp. 1571–1580, Sep. 2004). Linear region: erf is approximately straight only for ∣Δt∣≲σj\lvert\Delta t\rvert\lesssim\sigma_j∣Δt∣≲σj​ (⟨e⟩(σj)=0.683\langle e\rangle(\sigma_j)=0.683⟨e⟩(σj​)=0.683, ⟨e⟩(2σj)=0.954\langle e\rangle(2\sigma_j)=0.954⟨e⟩(2σj​)=0.954 is already saturated); the tangent meets ±1\pm1±1 at Δt=±σjπ/2\Delta t=\pm\sigma_j\sqrt{\pi/2}Δt=±σj​π/2​. Larger errors enter the slew-limited region — where the −20-20−20 dB/dec JTOL segment of Step 4 lives. Transition density: only transitions update the loop, so the average gain is further multiplied by ρT\rho_TρT​ (≈0.5\approx0.5≈0.5 for random data). Worked example (site values): take the rms jitter between data edge and clock as this site's canonical example C, σt=447.9\sigma_t=447.9σt​=447.9 fs (free-running 5 GHz VCO, −100-100−100 dBc/Hz @ 1 MHz, integrated 1→100 MHz; used here as a representative σj\sigma_jσj​), UI =40=40=40 ps (25 Gb/s NRZ, as in final_exam problem 10). Kbb=2π⋅1447.9×10−15 s=0.79794.479×10−13 s=1.78×1012 s−1,Kbb⋅UI=1.78×1012×40×10−12=71.3 (per UI).K_{bb}=\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}\cdot\frac{1}{447.9\times10^{-15}\ \text{s}} =\frac{0.7979}{4.479\times10^{-13}\ \text{s}}=1.78\times10^{12}\ \text{s}^{-1}, \qquad K_{bb}\cdot\text{UI}=1.78\times10^{12}\times40\times10^{-12}=71.3\ \text{(per UI)}.Kbb​=π2​​⋅447.9×10−15 s1​=4.479×10−13 s0.7979​=1.78×1012 s−1,Kbb​⋅UI=1.78×1012×40×10−12=71.3 (per UI). In other words the PD's expected output already hits ±1\pm1±1 when the clock is off by 1/71.3 UI=0.0141/71.3\ \text{UI}=0.0141/71.3 UI=0.014 UI =0.56=0.56=0.56 ps — the linear region is only half a picosecond wide. The smaller the σt\sigma_tσt​ the ISF gives (the cleaner the VCO), the larger KbbK_{bb}Kbb​ and the faster the loop — but the narrower the linear region: this is where bang-bang differs most from a linear PLL. import numpy as np from scipy.special import erf sigma_t = 447.9e-15 # s, canonical example C (free-running VCO, 1-100 MHz) UI = 40e-12 # s, 25 Gb/s NRZ K_bb = np.sqrt(2/np.pi)/sigma_t print(f"{K_bb:.3e}", round(K_bb*UI, 1)) # -> 1.781e+12 71.3 d = 1e-18 # numerical derivative of erf(dt/(sqrt2 sigma)) at 0 slope = (erf(d/(np.sqrt(2)*sigma_t)) - erf(-d/(np.sqrt(2)*sigma_t)))/(2*d) print(f"{slope:.3e}", round(sigma_t*np.sqrt(np.pi/2)*1e12, 3)) # -> 1.781e+12 0.561

documents.t: Most modern SerDes CDRs have no VCO in the loop: a shared PLL generates fixed-frequency multi-phase clocks, and the CDR uses a phase interpolator (PI) to interpolate the sampling clock between those phases. The PI is driven by a bbb-bit phase code; one UI is divided into 2b2^b2b steps: ΔϕPI=UI2b(b=6: 40 ps64=0.625 ps=0.0156 UI).\Delta\phi_{PI}=\frac{\text{UI}}{2^b}\qquad(b=6:\ \frac{40\ \text{ps}}{64}=0.625\ \text{ps}=0.0156\ \text{UI}).ΔϕPI​=2bUI​(b=6: 6440 ps​=0.625 ps=0.0156 UI). The simplest first-order bang-bang loop pushes the phase code one step in the direction the PD indicates every update period Tu=Ndec⋅UIT_u=N_{dec}\cdot\text{UI}Tu​=Ndec​⋅UI (NdecN_{dec}Ndec​ is the decimation/voting factor applied to the PD output): ϕ[k+1]=ϕ[k]+Kp sign(e[k]),Kp=m⋅ΔϕPI (m LSBs).\phi[k+1]=\phi[k]+K_p\,\text{sign}(e[k]),\qquad K_p=m\cdot\Delta\phi_{PI}\ (m\ \text{LSBs}).ϕ[k+1]=ϕ[k]+Kp​sign(e[k]),Kp​=m⋅ΔϕPI​ (m LSBs). Three consequences of discretization (external literature, not among this site's five PDFs: R. C. Walker, "Designing Bang-Bang PLLs for Clock and Data Recovery in Serial Data Transmission Systems," in Phase-Locking in High-Performance Systems, B. Razavi, Ed., IEEE Press, 2003): Hunting (limit cycle): once locked, the PD still only says "early" or "late," so the phase code hops back and forth around the optimum, producing a deterministic jitter of peak-to-peak KpK_pKp​; if the loop has a latency of DDD update periods (the pipeline between decision and execution), the phase overshoots by DDD extra steps before reversing and the limit cycle grows to peak-to-peak (2D+1)Kp(2D+1)K_p(2D+1)Kp​ (counted directly with the noise-free model in the Python below). This is a DJ: in the TJ budget it enters as DJpp\text{DJ}_{pp}DJpp​, added directly, not scaled with BER (see dj_dual_dirac). Quantization noise: treating the PI phase error as uniformly distributed, its rms is ΔϕPI/12=0.18\Delta\phi_{PI}/\sqrt{12}=0.18ΔϕPI​/12​=0.18 ps — the same order as σt=0.45\sigma_t=0.45σt​=0.45 ps, not negligible. Linearized bandwidth: substituting KbbK_{bb}Kbb​ from Step 2, the phase correction per update is ≈KpKbbρT Δt\approx K_p K_{bb}\rho_T\,\Delta t≈Kp​Kbb​ρT​Δt, and the continuous-time approximation gives a first-order loop dϕclkdt≈KpKbbρTTu (ϕdata−ϕclk) ⇒ fBW≈KpKbbρTfu2π,fu=1Tu.\frac{d\phi_{clk}}{dt}\approx\frac{K_pK_{bb}\rho_T}{T_u}\,(\phi_{data}-\phi_{clk}) \ \Rightarrow\ f_{BW}\approx\frac{K_pK_{bb}\rho_T f_u}{2\pi},\qquad f_u=\frac{1}{T_u}.dtdϕclk​​≈Tu​Kp​Kbb​ρT​​(ϕdata​−ϕclk​) ⇒ fBW​≈2πKp​Kbb​ρT​fu​​,fu​=Tu​1​. Dimension check: KpK_pKp​ [s] ×Kbb\times K_{bb}×Kbb​ [1/s] ×fu\times f_u×fu​ [1/s] === [1/s] ✓; KpKbbK_pK_{bb}Kp​Kbb​ is the (dimensionless) "loop gain per update"; the discrete loop needs KpKbbρT<2K_pK_{bb}\rho_T\lt2Kp​Kbb​ρT​<2 for stability, and the linearization itself holds only when Kp≲σjK_p\lesssim\sigma_jKp​≲σj​ (step smaller than the noise). Worked (site values): Kp=1K_p=1Kp​=1 LSB =0.625=0.625=0.625 ps, Kbb=1.78×1012K_{bb}=1.78\times10^{12}Kbb​=1.78×1012 s−1^{-1}−1, ρT=0.5\rho_T=0.5ρT​=0.5. Ndec=1N_{dec}=1Ndec​=1 (update every UI): KpKbb=1.11K_pK_{bb}=1.11Kp​Kbb​=1.11 per update — already beyond what the linearization can describe (the 0.6250.6250.625 ps step exceeds σj=0.448\sigma_j=0.448σj​=0.448 ps), so the nominal fBW=2.2f_{BW}=2.2fBW​=2.2 GHz is meaningless; Ndec=16N_{dec}=16Ndec​=16 (fu=1.5625f_u=1.5625fu​=1.5625 GHz): fBW≈0.5×0.625 ps×1.78×1012 s−1×1.5625×109 s−1/2π=138f_{BW}\approx0.5\times0.625\text{ ps}\times1.78\times10^{12}\text{ s}^{-1} \times1.5625\times10^9\text{ s}^{-1}/2\pi=138fBW​≈0.5×0.625 ps×1.78×1012 s−1×1.5625×109 s−1/2π=138 MHz, a typical CDR-bandwidth order of magnitude. Honest statement: here Kp≈σjK_p\approx\sigma_jKp​≈σj​, so hunting pushes the effective σj\sigma_jσj​ up and KbbK_{bb}Kbb​ down; the exact value needs Monte-Carlo (a v12 lab); this page gives only the order of magnitude. Slew capability of the proportional path: at most (Kp/UI) fu(K_p/\text{UI})\,f_u(Kp​/UI)fu​ UI per second, i.e. a trackable frequency offset of (Kp/UI) fu/fb(K_p/\text{UI})\,f_u/f_b(Kp​/UI)fu​/fb​: 1/64=15 6251/64=15\,6251/64=15625 ppm for Ndec=1N_{dec}=1Ndec​=1, 977977977 ppm for Ndec=16N_{dec}=16Ndec​=16. Step 5 compares this against the 5000 ppm of SSC. import numpy as np fb, UI, b = 25e9, 40e-12, 6 Kp = UI/2**b print(round(Kp*1e12, 3), round(Kp/UI, 4), round(Kp/np.sqrt(12)*1e12, 3)) # -> 0.625 0.0156 0.18 K_bb = np.sqrt(2/np.pi)/447.9e-15 for Ndec in (1, 16): fu = fb/Ndec f_bw = 0.5*Kp*K_bb*fu/(2*np.pi) # rho_T = 0.5 (random data); one sign per update, no voting print(Ndec, f"{f_bw:.3e}", f"{(Kp/UI)*fu/fb*1e6:.0f}") # -> 1 2.215e+09 15625 # -> 16 1.384e+08 977 def hunting_pp(D, n=400): # noise-free limit cycle, latency D updates, units of Kp phi, q, hist = 0.3, [0.0]*D, [] for k in range(n): q.append(-np.sign(phi) if phi != 0 else 1.0) phi += q.pop(0) hist.append(phi) h = np.array(hist[n//2:]) return float(h.max() - h.min()) print([hunting_pp(D) for D in (0, 1, 2, 4)]) # -> [1.0, 3.0, 5.0, 9.0] Sidebar: why a DLL does not "accumulate" jitter (external literature, not among this site's five PDFs: J. G. Maneatis, "Low-Jitter Process-Independent DLL and PLL Based on Self-Biased Techniques," IEEE J. Solid-State Circuits, vol. 31, no. 11, pp. 1723–1732, Nov. 1996). The PI architecture above is really DLL (delay-locked loop) thinking: there is no oscillator in the loop, only "a delay relative to the reference clock." An oscillator's phase is the integral of its frequency, so white noise → phase random walk → σΔt=κΔt\sigma_{\Delta t}=\kappa\sqrt{\Delta t}σΔt​=κΔt​ ([P2] Eq.(8), p.792, see lc_vs_ring); a delay line's error is re-zeroed by the reference edge every cycle, so noise is added once and never accumulates. The price is that the output jitter inherits the reference clock's jitter directly (there is no high-pass to filter it) and there is no frequency degree of freedom — so "frequency tracking" in a PI-CDR relies entirely on the integral path of Step 5 accumulating the phase code digitally.

Given an eye margin UI−TJeye\text{UI}-\text{TJ}_{eye}UI−TJeye​, the tolerable single-tone sinusoidal input jitter is JTOLpp(f)=UI−TJeye∣1−H(f)∣ \boxed{\ \text{JTOL}_{pp}(f)=\frac{\text{UI}-\text{TJ}_{eye}}{\lvert1-H(f)\rvert}\ } JTOLpp​(f)=∣1−H(f)∣UI−TJeye​​ ​ ⚠️ Convention flag (peak vs peak-to-peak, a factor of 2): industry JTOL masks are specified peak-to-peak (UI pp). The actual mask is the lower envelope (min) of the three. This is why datasheet JTOL curves look the way they do: −40-40−40 at low frequency, −20-20−20 in the middle, a plateau at high frequency — each segment corresponds to a different mechanism in the loop. with ζ=0.707\zeta=0.707ζ=0.707 the zero fz=707f_z=707fz​=707 kHz sits almost on fnf_nfn​, so no −20-20−20 segment is visible; raising ζ\zetaζ to 4 (fz=125f_z=125fz​=125 kHz) turns the 100 kHz→1 MHz slope into −24-24−24 dB/dec — one origin of the −20-20−20 dB/dec mid-segment in specifications. import numpy as np from simulations.common.pll_utils import H_highpass_mag2 UI, sigma_t, qinv = 40e-12, 447.9e-15, 7.03 TJ_eye = 2*qinv*sigma_t margin_UI = 1 - TJ_eye/UI print(round(TJ_eye*1e12, 2), round(TJ_eye/UI, 3), round(margin_UI, 3)) # -> 6.3 0.157 0.843 fn, zeta = 1e6, 0.707 for f in [1e4, 3e4, 1e5, 1e6, 1e7]: H_hp = np.sqrt(H_highpass_mag2(np.array([f]), fn, zeta)[0]) # amplitude |1-H_lp| print(f"{f:.0e}", f"{H_hp:.3e}", round(margin_UI/H_hp, 2)) # -> 1e+04 1.000e-04 8425.63 # -> 3e+04 9.000e-04 936.18 # -> 1e+05 1.000e-02 84.26 # -> 1e+06 7.072e-01 1.19 # -> 1e+07 1.000e+00 0.84 def jtol_slope(zeta, fa, fb): # dB per decade of JTOL between fa and fb = 10 fa Ha, Hb = (np.sqrt(H_highpass_mag2(np.array([x]), fn, zeta)[0]) for x in (fa, fb)) return float(20*np.log10((margin_UI/Hb)/(margin_UI/Ha))) for zeta in (0.707, 4.0): print(zeta, [round(jtol_slope(zeta, fa, 10*fa), 1) for fa in (1e4, 1e5, 1e6)]) # -> 0.707 [-40.0, -37.0, -3.0] # -> 4.0 [-37.9, -24.0, -16.0] Dimension check: UI−TJeye\text{UI}-\text{TJ}_{eye}UI−TJeye​ [UI] ÷ a dimensionless amplitude transfer === [UI] ✓; documents.t: Spread-spectrum clocking (SSC) deliberately sweeps the transmitter clock frequency as a triangle wave at fm≈30f_m\approx30fm​≈30–333333 kHz from nominal down to −δ-\delta−δ (down-spread, PCIe-style δ=0.5%\delta=0.5\%δ=0.5%; PCI Express Base Specification, version to be verified; external literature, not among this site's five PDFs) to spread EMI energy. To the receiver's CDR this is not noise but a deterministic FM that must be tracked — especially when the RX reference clock is not spread along with it (separate-reference architectures). Deriving the peak-to-peak phase step by step. Let the bit rate be fbf_bfb​; the frequency offset relative to the center value is a triangle wave of amplitude ±δfb/2\pm\delta f_b/2±δfb​/2 and period Tm=1/fmT_m=1/f_mTm​=1/fm​. The phase (in UI) is the integral of the frequency offset; the area of the triangle's positive half-period is 12⋅Tm2⋅δfb2=δfbTm8\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac{T_m}{2}\cdot\tfrac{\delta f_b}{2}=\dfrac{\delta f_bT_m}{8}21​⋅2Tm​​⋅2δfb​​=8δfb​Tm​​, which is the peak-to-peak phase: Δϕpp=δ fb Tm8 UI=14 Tm Δfpk cycles (Δfpk=δfclk/2 is the clock’s peak frequency deviation).\boxed{\ \Delta\phi_{pp}=\frac{\delta\,f_b\,T_m}{8}\ \text{UI} =\frac{1}{4}\,T_m\,\Delta f_{pk}\ \text{cycles}\ }\qquad(\Delta f_{pk}=\delta f_{clk}/2\ \text{is the clock's peak frequency deviation}). Δϕpp​=8δfb​Tm​​ UI=41​Tm​Δfpk​ cycles ​(Δfpk​=δfclk​/2 is the clock’s peak frequency deviation). Substituting fb=25f_b=25fb​=25 Gb/s (half-rate clock fclk=12.5f_{clk}=12.5fclk​=12.5 GHz), δ=0.005\delta=0.005δ=0.005, fm=30f_m=30fm​=30 kHz (Tm=33.3T_m=33.3Tm​=33.3 µs): Δfpk=0.005×12.5 GHz2=31.25 MHz,Δϕpp=14×33.3 μs×31.25 MHz=260 cycles=260×80 ps=20.8 ns=521 UI.\Delta f_{pk}=\frac{0.005\times12.5\ \text{GHz}}{2}=31.25\ \text{MHz},\quad \Delta\phi_{pp}=\tfrac14\times33.3\ \mu\text{s}\times31.25\ \text{MHz}=260\ \text{cycles} =260\times80\ \text{ps}=20.8\ \text{ns}=521\ \text{UI}.Δfpk​=20.005×12.5 GHz​=31.25 MHz,Δϕpp​=41​×33.3 μs×31.25 MHz=260 cycles=260×80 ps=20.8 ns=521 UI. Dimension check: [s]×[1/s]=[\text{s}]\times[\text{1/s}]=[s]×[1/s]= dimensionless (a cycle count) ✓; one 12.5 GHz cycle =2=2=2 UI ✓. This is a phase excursion of over five hundred UI, four orders of magnitude larger than any RJ. The Step-4 mask must give JTOL>521\text{JTOL}\gt521JTOL>521 UI at 30 kHz: type-II with fn=1f_n=1fn​=1 MHz gives 936936936 UI ✓ (and 8.4×1038.4\times10^38.4×103 UI at 10 kHz). documents.t: Prerequisites: psd_phase_noise_jitter (SϕS_\phiSϕ​, L\mathcal{L}L, phase↔time conversion), pll_noise_budget (∣Hlp∣2,∣Hhp∣2\lvert H_{lp}\rvert^2,\lvert H_{hp}\rvert^2∣Hlp​∣2,∣Hhp​∣2 and the five-source budget — this page reuses them directly, no re-derivation), white_noise_to_phase_noise (where the VCO's −148-148−148 dBc/Hz comes from) | Next: serdes_clocking_connection, exercises In a real system there is no such thing as "one oscillator, used directly": the reference crystal is multiplied up by a PLL, divided back down by dividers, and passes through several buffer stages before reaching the sampler. The system engineer's daily question is: given the source L(f)\mathcal{L}(f)L(f), what is L(f)\mathcal{L}(f)L(f) at every node of the clock tree? What is the integrated jitter of the final clock? The good news: bookkeeping for the entire chain needs only five rules. This page derives each of the five rules step by step (no skipped steps, with units, with failure conditions), then strings them together in one complete worked chain, computed all the way to the end. Physical intuition (conclusion first): only two kinds of things ever happen to phase along a clock chain — (1) Deterministic phase scaling: ×N multiplies phase by NNN (+20log⁡10N+20\log_{10}N+20log10​N dB), ÷N divides phase by NNN (−20log⁡10N-20\log_{10}N−20log10​N dB), a PLL applies ×N to the reference in-band and low-passes it, and high-passes the VCO. Scaling acts on the entire curve; the offset axis does not move. (2) Additive independent noise: the buffer's and divider's own noise floor, uncorrelated with the input phase, adds in power (never in dB). There is also one beautiful conserved quantity: under ideal ×N/÷N, the time jitter σt\sigma_tσt​ in seconds is exactly unchanged — what changes is only "what angular fraction of one period the same error in seconds occupies".

The worked chain's VCO anchor of −148-148−148 dBc/Hz @ 1 MHz is the site's canonical example B, using the "/4" SSB accounting of [P1] Eq.(21), p.185; the clean time-domain derivation's "/2" version gives −145-145−145 (the famous 3 dB convention dispute, see white_noise_to_phase_noise). The four rules on this page (±20log⁡10N\pm20\log_{10}N±20log10​N, power addition) are themselves ratio operations: as long as input and output use the same convention, /2 or /4 cancels, and the rules' numbers are convention-independent — which is why the accounting rules can safely be used as a lookup table.

documents.t: Step 1 (write the signal as a function of phase). Using the decomposition of [P1] Eq.(1), p.180, take a sinusoidal waveform: Vin(t)=cos⁡(Φin(t)),Φin(t)=ωref t+ϕin(t)V_{in}(t)=\cos\big(\Phi_{in}(t)\big),\qquad \Phi_{in}(t)=\omega_{ref}\,t+\phi_{in}(t)Vin​(t)=cos(Φin​(t)),Φin​(t)=ωref​t+ϕin​(t) Φin\Phi_{in}Φin​ is the total phase (rad), ϕin\phi_{in}ϕin​ is the excess phase (rad), ωref=2πfref\omega_{ref}=2\pi f_{ref}ωref​=2πfref​ (rad/s). Step 2 (ideal multiplier = memoryless nonlinearity + bandpass). Any memoryless nonlinearity g(⋅)g(\cdot)g(⋅) acting on cos⁡Φ\cos\PhicosΦ: because g(cos⁡Φ)g(\cos\Phi)g(cosΦ) is a 2π2\pi2π-periodic function of Φ\PhiΦ, it can be expanded as a Fourier series in Φ\PhiΦ: g(cos⁡Φ(t))=∑k=0∞akcos⁡(k Φ(t)+θk)g\big(\cos\Phi(t)\big)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}a_k\cos\big(k\,\Phi(t)+\theta_k\big)g(cosΦ(t))=k=0∑∞​ak​cos(kΦ(t)+θk​) The key is the argument: every term is "an integer multiple of the instantaneous total phase, kΦ(t)k\Phi(t)kΦ(t)" — a memoryless element has no notion of time, it can only act on "the phase right now", so the excess phase is carried along completely intact. Step 3 (bandpass selects the NNN-th harmonic). A bandpass filter centered at NfrefN f_{ref}Nfref​ picks the k=Nk=Nk=N term: Vout(t)∝cos⁡(NΦin(t))=cos⁡(Nωref t+Nϕin(t))⟹ ϕout(t)=N ϕin(t) V_{out}(t)\propto\cos\big(N\Phi_{in}(t)\big)=\cos\big(N\omega_{ref}\,t+N\phi_{in}(t)\big) \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \boxed{\ \phi_{out}(t)=N\,\phi_{in}(t)\ }Vout​(t)∝cos(NΦin​(t))=cos(Nωref​t+Nϕin​(t))⟹ ϕout​(t)=Nϕin​(t) ​ This identity holds instant by instant — every frequency component of ϕin\phi_{in}ϕin​ is multiplied by NNN, with no frequency selectivity whatsoever. Step 4 (convert to PSD and dB). Phase multiplied by NNN (amplitude), power spectral density multiplied by N2N^2N2: Sϕ,out(f)=N2 Sϕ,in(f) [rad2/Hz],Lout(f)=Lin(f)+20log⁡10N [dBc/Hz]S_{\phi,out}(f)=N^2\,S_{\phi,in}(f)\ \ [\text{rad}^2/\text{Hz}],\qquad \mathcal{L}_{out}(f)=\mathcal{L}_{in}(f)+20\log_{10}N\ \ [\text{dBc/Hz}]Sϕ,out​(f)=N2Sϕ,in​(f) [rad2/Hz],Lout​(f)=Lin​(f)+20log10​N [dBc/Hz] The second equation used L=12Sϕ\mathcal{L}=\tfrac12 S_\phiL=21​Sϕ​ — input and output use the same convention, the 12\tfrac1221​ cancels, so +20log⁡10N+20\log_{10}N+20log10​N is independent of the /2-vs-/4 convention. For N=50N=50N=50, +20log⁡1050=+33.98+20\log_{10}50=+33.98+20log10​50=+33.98 dB ≈+34\approx+34≈+34 dB. Physical meaning: multiplication creates no noise. It magnifies "the same absolute time jitter" into an NNN-times larger angle — one output period is only 1/N1/N1/N as long as the input's, so the same error in seconds occupies NNN times the fraction of an output period. The offset axis does not move (common mistake): what gets multiplied by NNN is the phase amplitude, not the rhythm of the phase fluctuations. The entire L\mathcal{L}L curve shifts vertically up by 20log⁡10N20\log_{10}N20log10​N; the horizontal axis (offset fff) is completely unchanged. Dimension check: NNN dimensionless, ϕ\phiϕ in rad, SϕS_\phiSϕ​ in rad²/Hz, 20log⁡10N20\log_{10}N20log10​N in dB ✓. Time-jitter conservation: Δtout=ϕout2πNfref=Nϕin2πNfref=ϕin2πfref=Δtin\Delta t_{out}=\dfrac{\phi_{out}}{2\pi N f_{ref}}=\dfrac{N\phi_{in}}{2\pi N f_{ref}} =\dfrac{\phi_{in}}{2\pi f_{ref}}=\Delta t_{in}Δtout​=2πNfref​ϕout​​=2πNfref​Nϕin​​=2πfref​ϕin​​=Δtin​ — the edge error in seconds is unchanged (verified numerically in Step 5 below). Failure conditions: (1) small-angle approximation — σϕ,out=Nσϕ,in\sigma_{\phi,out}=N\sigma_{\phi,in}σϕ,out​=Nσϕ,in​; for large NNN (e.g. N=1000N=1000N=1000, +60+60+60 dB) it can approach 1 rad, L≈12Sϕ\mathcal{L}\approx\tfrac12 S_\phiL≈21​Sϕ​ collapses, and the carrier energy redistributes into a Lorentzian (the linewidth diffusion constant DDD is magnified by N2N^2N2, see lorentzian_linewidth); (2) sideband overlap — for offsets near fref/2f_{ref}/2fref​/2 the skirts of the N±1N\pm1N±1 harmonics mix into the bandpass; (3) real multipliers have their own additive floor (Rule 4). ILCM addendum: this rule assumes a "memoryless nonlinearity + bandpass" — that kind of multiplier creates no noise; it just scales the input's excess phase by NNN, unchanged. A real injection-locked clock multiplier (ILCM) is not that machine: it is a locked oscillator, so the carrier path is still deterministically ϕout≈Nϕin\phi_{out}\approx N\phi_{in}ϕout​≈Nϕin​ (in-band reference noise still eats N2SrefN^2S_{ref}N2Sref​, +20log⁡10N+20\log_{10}N+20log10​N, consistent with this rule) — but its own free-running phase noise is high-pass shaped by a first-order discrete-time loop (corner ≈βfref/2π\approx\beta f_{ref}/2\pi≈βfref​/2π, where β\betaβ is the realignment factor per reference pulse), replacing this rule's "clean constant shift" assumption. Past the corner, the output noise is set by the ILCM's own oscillator quality — no longer something +20log⁡10N+20\log_{10}N+20log10​N describes. Full derivation: subharmonic_injection.

documents.t: The quadrature_and_coupled_oscillators page, in the ÷2-generates-I/Q section, directly cites Lout=Lin−20log⁡10N\mathcal{L}_{out}=\mathcal{L}_{in}-20\log_{10}NLout​=Lin​−20log10​N; this is the rigorous derivation's home for that equation, and the two pages' numbers agree (÷2 is −6.02-6.02−6.02 dB). Step 1 (timing of the input edges). The kkk-th input rising zero crossing tkt_ktk​ is defined by the total phase: Φin(tk)=2πk\Phi_{in}(t_k)=2\pi kΦin​(tk​)=2πk. Substituting Φin=ωreft+ϕin(t)\Phi_{in}=\omega_{ref}t+\phi_{in}(t)Φin​=ωref​t+ϕin​(t) and solving: tk=k Tref−ϕin(tk)ωref⟹δtk=−ϕin(kTref)ωreft_k=k\,T_{ref}-\frac{\phi_{in}(t_k)}{\omega_{ref}} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \delta t_k=-\frac{\phi_{in}(kT_{ref})}{\omega_{ref}}tk​=kTref​−ωref​ϕin​(tk​)​⟹δtk​=−ωref​ϕin​(kTref​)​ The second equation used "ϕ\phiϕ slowly varying" (offset ≪fref\ll f_{ref}≪fref​) to replace ϕin(tk)\phi_{in}(t_k)ϕin​(tk​) with ϕin(kTref)\phi_{in}(kT_{ref})ϕin​(kTref​). Dimension check: [rad]/[rad/s]=[s][\text{rad}]/[\text{rad/s}]=[\text{s}][rad]/[rad/s]=[s] ✓. Step 2 (a divider only drops edges, never moves them). An ideal ÷N is an edge-picking machine: for every NNN input edges it outputs one, and the output edge's time is exactly the time of the selected input edge. So the absolute time error δt\delta tδt passes to the output completely intact: δtm(out)=δtmN\delta t^{(out)}_m=\delta t_{mN}δtm(out)​=δtmN​ Step 3 (fold the time error back into the output carrier's phase). The output carrier is ωout=ωref/N\omega_{out}=\omega_{ref}/Nωout​=ωref​/N. The output excess phase follows from the same phase definition in reverse (Φout(tm′)=2πm\Phi_{out}(t'_m)=2\pi mΦout​(tm′​)=2πm, tm′=mTout+δtmt'_m=mT_{out}+\delta t_mtm′​=mTout​+δtm​): ϕout=− ωout δt(out)=ωoutωref ϕin⟹ ϕout=ϕinN \phi_{out}=-\,\omega_{out}\,\delta t^{(out)} =\frac{\omega_{out}}{\omega_{ref}}\,\phi_{in} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \boxed{\ \phi_{out}=\frac{\phi_{in}}{N}\ }ϕout​=−ωout​δt(out)=ωref​ωout​​ϕin​⟹ ϕout​=Nϕin​​ ​ Step 4 (PSD and dB). Sϕ,out(f)=Sϕ,in(f)N2,Lout(f)=Lin(f)−20log⁡10NS_{\phi,out}(f)=\frac{S_{\phi,in}(f)}{N^2},\qquad \mathcal{L}_{out}(f)=\mathcal{L}_{in}(f)-20\log_{10}NSϕ,out​(f)=N2Sϕ,in​(f)​,Lout​(f)=Lin​(f)−20log10​N ÷2 is −20log⁡102=−6.02-20\log_{10}2=-6.02−20log10​2=−6.02 dB. Physical meaning: the same jitter in seconds, spread over a period NNN times longer, is an angle NNN times smaller. Perfectly symmetric with Rule 1: ×N then ÷N brings L\mathcal{L}L back to where it started, and σt\sigma_tσt​ (seconds) is unchanged throughout. Quick check (work it out yourself, then check) Try it yourself first: the change in L(f) from an ideal ÷4 divider (not the ÷2 used in this section's example) = ? (answer in dB, include the sign) dBCheckShow answer Graded correct within ±1% relative error; scientific notation is accepted. Failure conditions (both matter): Sampling foldover (aliasing): ϕout\phi_{out}ϕout​ is defined only at the output edge instants — this is a system sampled at ∼fout\sim f_{out}∼fout​. Components of the input phase noise at offsets above ∼fout/2\sim f_{out}/2∼fout​/2 fold back into the output band; for a flat wideband noise floor, division does not earn the full 20log⁡10N20\log_{10}N20log10​N (foldover stacks the power back). The clean −20log⁡10N-20\log_{10}N−20log10​N holds only for close-in noise at offsets ≪fout\ll f_{out}≪fout​. (External literature, not among the five source PDFs; for the standard divider noise model see Egan at the end of this page.) The divider's own floor: real dividers (CML latch, TSPC) have their own additive floor (Rule 4), often higher than "the cleanly divided-down signal" — after division the output can never be better than the divider's own floor. Relation to [P4]: an injection-locked frequency divider (ILFD) uses the ISF's 2nd harmonic to lock 2f02f_02f0​ to f0f_0f0​, implementing ÷2 ([P4], frequency division in Part II, see paper_004). The ÷N phase accounting (ϕ/N\phi/Nϕ/N) holds equally for the ILFD's carrier path; but an ILFD near the edge of its lock range has its own noise behavior, outside this page's ideal accounting.

documents.t: A PLL is the closed-loop implementation of Rule 1: the divider brings the output back to freff_{ref}fref​ for phase comparison, which forces "output phase =N×=N\times=N× reference phase" — so reference noise first takes +20log⁡10N+20\log_{10}N+20log10​N (Rule 1), and is then shaped by the closed-loop lowpass ∣Hlp∣2\lvert H_{lp}\rvert^2∣Hlp​∣2; the VCO's own noise is shaped by the highpass ∣Hhp∣2\lvert H_{hp}\rvert^2∣Hhp​∣2: Sout(f)=N2 Sref(f) ∣Hlp(f)∣2+Svco(f) ∣Hhp(f)∣2[rad2/Hz]S_{out}(f)=N^2\,S_{ref}(f)\,\lvert H_{lp}(f)\rvert^2+S_{vco}(f)\,\lvert H_{hp}(f)\rvert^2 \qquad[\text{rad}^2/\text{Hz}]Sout​(f)=N2Sref​(f)∣Hlp​(f)∣2+Svco​(f)∣Hhp​(f)∣2[rad2/Hz] The two transfer functions (type-II second order, ωn,ζ\omega_n,\zetaωn​,ζ) and the full five-source budget were derived step by step and verified in pll_noise_budget; this page reuses them directly without re-deriving (that page also includes the charge-pump floor Scp∣Hlp∣2S_{cp}\lvert H_{lp}\rvert^2Scp​∣Hlp​∣2; to keep this page's worked chain focused on the four rules, the CP floor is folded conceptually into the "in-band floor" and omitted numerically, marked illustrative). The brick-wall accounting used for the lookup table is its asymptotic version: in-band (f≪fnf\ll f_nf≪fn​): ∣Hlp∣2→1\lvert H_{lp}\rvert^2\to1∣Hlp​∣2→1, ∣Hhp∣2→0\lvert H_{hp}\rvert^2\to0∣Hhp​∣2→0 ⇒ Lout≈Lref+20log⁡10N\mathcal{L}_{out}\approx\mathcal{L}_{ref}+20\log_{10}NLout​≈Lref​+20log10​N. out-of-band (f≫fnf\gg f_nf≫fn​): ∣Hlp∣2→0\lvert H_{lp}\rvert^2\to0∣Hlp​∣2→0, ∣Hhp∣2→1\lvert H_{hp}\rvert^2\to1∣Hhp​∣2→1 ⇒ Lout≈Lvco\mathcal{L}_{out}\approx\mathcal{L}_{vco}Lout​≈Lvco​ (the free-running VCO skirt). Take the crossover at the loop bandwidth fnf_nfn​. Dimension check: all SSS in rad²/Hz, N2N^2N2 and ∣H∣2\lvert H\rvert^2∣H∣2 dimensionless ✓. The brick-wall version is convenient but has one famous trap — the pure second-order loop's reference tail, laid out numerically in Step 6.
documents.s: Rule 3: through a PLL — the reference goes "×N + lowpass", the VCO goes "highpass"

documents.t: Step 1 (why a buffer is "additive"). A buffer regenerates edges: at the instant the input waveform crosses the switching threshold, the noise voltage vnv_nvn​ (V) of the buffer's internal devices sits on top of the threshold and displaces the output edge by Δtadd=vn(tk)SR[VV/s=s] ✓\Delta t_{add}=\frac{v_n(t_k)}{SR}\qquad \Big[\frac{\text{V}}{\text{V/s}}=\text{s}\Big]\ \checkmarkΔtadd​=SRvn​(tk​)​[V/sV​=s] ✓ (SRSRSR = slew rate at the threshold crossing, V/s. This is the same physics as waveform_slope's "most sensitive where the slope is small".) vnv_nvn​ comes from the buffer's own devices and is uncorrelated with the input clock's phase. Step 2 (uncorrelated ⇒ PSDs add). In phase this is pure addition: ϕout=ϕin+ϕadd⟹Sϕ,out(f)=Sϕ,in(f)+Sbuf(f)\phi_{out}=\phi_{in}+\phi_{add} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad S_{\phi,out}(f)=S_{\phi,in}(f)+S_{buf}(f)ϕout​=ϕin​+ϕadd​⟹Sϕ,out​(f)=Sϕ,in​(f)+Sbuf​(f) (The cross term ⟨ϕinϕadd⟩=0\langle\phi_{in}\phi_{add}\rangle=0⟨ϕin​ϕadd​⟩=0.) Converting to dBc/Hz gives the lookup-table formula — note you must convert to linear first, add, then convert back to dB: Lout(f)=10log⁡10(10Lin(f)/10+10Lbuf(f)/10) \boxed{\ \mathcal{L}_{out}(f)=10\log_{10}\Big(10^{\mathcal{L}_{in}(f)/10}+10^{\mathcal{L}_{buf}(f)/10}\Big)\ } Lout​(f)=10log10​(10Lin​(f)/10+10Lbuf​(f)/10) ​ Both L\mathcal{L}L are SSB on the same carrier with the same convention; the 12\tfrac1221​ of L=12Sϕ\mathcal{L}=\tfrac12 S_\phiL=21​Sϕ​ cancels on both sides — so accounting directly in L\mathcal{L}L is legitimate, independent of the /2-vs-/4 convention. Step 3 (multiplicative vs additive — the most important classification on this page). Rules 1–3 are multiplicative: they scale/shape the incoming phase curve as a whole; a clean source gives a clean output. Rule 4 is additive: the buffer injects new, independent noise, and the output can never be better than the buffer's own floor — however clean the source, one noisy buffer stage ruins it. That is what "floor dominates" means. Step 4 (when the floor takes over — the dB-addition table). Let the signal sit Δ\DeltaΔ dB above the floor; the penalty is 10log⁡10(1+10−Δ/10)10\log_{10}(1+10^{-\Delta/10})10log10​(1+10−Δ/10): Δ=Lin−Lbuf\Delta=\mathcal{L}_{in}-\mathcal{L}_{buf}Δ=Lin​−Lbuf​ Output above Lin\mathcal{L}_{in}Lin​ by Who dominates +20+20+20 dB (signal much higher) +0.04+0.04+0.04 dB floor completely invisible +10+10+10 dB +0.41+0.41+0.41 dB floor starting to show +6+6+6 dB +0.97+0.97+0.97 dB — +3+3+3 dB +1.76+1.76+1.76 dB — 000 dB (equal) +3.01+3.01+3.01 dB half and half −10-10−10 dB (signal below floor) output ≈Lbuf+0.41\approx\mathcal{L}_{buf}+0.41≈Lbuf​+0.41 floor dominates, output is clamped Step 5 (flat floor ⇒ white phase noise ⇒ one easy-to-remember jitter formula). A flat Lbuf\mathcal{L}_{buf}Lbuf​ is white phase noise; its own rms jitter contribution over an integration bandwidth BBB (Hz): σt,add=12πf02⋅10Lbuf/10⋅B\sigma_{t,add}=\frac{1}{2\pi f_0}\sqrt{2\cdot10^{\mathcal{L}_{buf}/10}\cdot B}σt,add​=2πf0​1​2⋅10Lbuf​/10⋅B​ (The 2×2\times2× is the small-angle L→Sϕ\mathcal{L}\to S_\phiL→Sϕ​ conversion, canonical formula 16; then integrate with canonical formula 19.) Numbers: Lbuf=−155\mathcal{L}_{buf}=-155Lbuf​=−155 dBc/Hz, B≈100B\approx100B≈100 MHz, f0=2.5f_0=2.5f0​=2.5 GHz: σt,add=2×3.16×10−16×108 /(2π×2.5×109)=2.51×10−4/1.571×1010=16.0\sigma_{t,add}=\sqrt{2\times3.16\times10^{-16}\times10^8}\,/(2\pi\times2.5\times10^9) =2.51\times10^{-4}/1.571\times10^{10}=16.0σt,add​=2×3.16×10−16×108​/(2π×2.5×109)=2.51×10−4/1.571×1010=16.0 fs. Dimension check: [rad2/Hz]⋅[Hz]=[rad]\sqrt{[\text{rad}^2/\text{Hz}]\cdot[\text{Hz}]}=[\text{rad}][rad2/Hz]⋅[Hz]​=[rad], [rad]/[rad/s]=[s][\text{rad}]/[\text{rad/s}]=[\text{s}][rad]/[rad/s]=[s] ✓. (This 16.0 fs will reappear, unchanged, in the worked chain's breakdown below.) Quick check (work it out yourself, then check) Try it yourself first: the same buffer (L_buf=−155 dBc/Hz, f₀=2.5 GHz), but with the integration bandwidth changed to B=200 MHz (twice the example above) — σ_t,add = ? (answer in fs) fsCheckShow answer Graded correct within ±2% relative error; scientific notation is accepted. The four rules' constants are first pinned down with a checkable Python block (the values after # -> are actual run output): import numpy as np print(round(20*np.log10(50), 2)) # -> 33.98 print(round(20*np.log10(2), 2)) # -> 6.02 print(round(10*np.log10(1 + 10**(-20/10)), 2)) # -> 0.04 print(round(10*np.log10(1 + 10**(-10/10)), 2)) # -> 0.41 print(round(10*np.log10(1 + 10**(-6/10)), 2)) # -> 0.97 print(round(10*np.log10(1 + 10**(-3/10)), 2)) # -> 1.76 print(round(10*np.log10(1 + 10**(0/10)), 2)) # -> 3.01
documents.s: Rule 4: the buffer/divider additive floor — power addition, never dB addition

documents.t: The question: Rules 1–4 cover "multiplication / division / PLL / buffer", but there is another component common in clock chains that this page has not yet accounted for — the DLL (delay-locked loop), and, right behind it, the phase interpolator (PI) that slices a coarse resolution finer still. A DLL is often assumed, by intuition, to be a "cheap PLL", but its noise behavior differs from a PLL / free-running VCO in kind, not just in degree: it is not a slower random walk, it is no random walk at all. This rule spells out the difference and adds PI quantization, a DJ (deterministic jitter) source that is easy to overlook in practice. Step 1 (why a DLL has no oscillator). The VCO inside a PLL is an integrator: a perturbation δv\delta vδv on the control voltage first becomes a frequency perturbation δω=KVCOδv\delta\omega=K_{VCO}\delta vδω=KVCO​δv, and frequency integrated over time is what becomes phase — once a perturbation happens, as long as the loop has not corrected it, the phase error stays there forever, and keeps accumulating going forward ([P2] Eq.(8), p.792's σΔt=κΔt\sigma_{\Delta t}=\kappa\sqrt{\Delta t}σΔt​=κΔt​ is the direct consequence of exactly this integration-plus-random-kicks picture). The delay line inside a DLL is not an oscillator — it is a feedforward element: the control voltage directly sets "how long this one edge gets delayed", with no integration over time involved. A delay error measured today is not handed to tomorrow, because every output edge corresponds to a brand-new reference edge making one pass through the delay line, not the same internal phase state rolling forward. That is the physical root of "no oscillator, no random walk". Step 2 (a single pass: the NNN-stage delay line's additive jitter, added in quadrature). The delay line is built from NNN stages (nominal delay Tref/NT_{ref}/NTref​/N each). Same mechanism as Rule 4's Step 1 — near each stage's switching threshold, device noise voltage vnv_nvn​ displaces that stage's output edge by Δtstage=vn/SR\Delta t_{stage}=v_n/SRΔtstage​=vn​/SR (units: s) — and the σstage\sigma_{stage}σstage​ of the iii-th stage are uncorrelated with each other (different devices, different noise sources). One reference edge that walks through all NNN stages picks up the power sum of NNN independent contributions (the same "PSDs add" logic as Rule 4's Step 2): σt,DLL2=N σstage2⟹σt,DLL=N σstage\sigma_{t,DLL}^2=N\,\sigma_{stage}^2 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \sigma_{t,DLL}=\sqrt{N}\,\sigma_{stage}σt,DLL2​=Nσstage2​⟹σt,DLL​=N​σstage​ Dimension check: N\sqrt{N}N​ dimensionless, [s]×[−]=[s][\text{s}]\times[-]=[\text{s}][s]×[−]=[s] ✓. Step 3 (add the reference's own jitter, freshly zeroed for every reference edge). The output edge's total time error is "this reference edge's own error σref\sigma_{ref}σref​" plus "the NNN-stage noise picked up on this one pass through the delay line", uncorrelated (different sources): σt,out2=σref2+N σstage2 \boxed{\ \sigma_{t,out}^2=\sigma_{ref}^2+N\,\sigma_{stage}^2\ } σt,out2​=σref2​+Nσstage2​ ​ The key point: when the next reference edge arrives, the delay line's NNN-stage noise is re-sampled independently (device thermal noise at the next switching instant has no memory of this one), and σref\sigma_{ref}σref​ is likewise the (different) next reference cycle's own error — the output jitter does not grow just because you count more cycles; σt,out\sigma_{t,out}σt,out​ is the same expression for every single output edge, regardless of "which cycle this is" or "how long since the last measurement point". Contrast this with the PLL / free-running VCO's σΔt=κΔt\sigma_{\Delta t}=\kappa\sqrt{\Delta t}σΔt​=κΔt​: there, Δt\Delta tΔt sits inside the square root, and the error grows the longer the measurement interval, because the same oscillator's phase state is dragged along by the integration the whole way. Here in the DLL there is no Δt\Delta tΔt, because there simply is no "phase state being dragged along by integration" to speak of — it is bounded. This is the core contrast this rule makes. Step 4 (first-order loop shaping does not change the "no accumulation" fact). A DLL is still a negative-feedback loop: a phase detector compares "the delay line's output edge" against "the reference edge" and drives the delay line's control voltage to lock the total delay to TrefT_{ref}Tref​ (this is exactly the topology of Maneatis's 1996 self-biased DLL). This feedback loop itself is usually first order (a single integrator/capacitor, without the VCO's second-order dynamics), with closed-loop transfer function HDLL(s)=ωDLLs+ωDLLH_{DLL}(s)=\frac{\omega_{DLL}}{s+\omega_{DLL}}HDLL​(s)=s+ωDLL​ωDLL​​ Low-pass for reference noise — within the loop bandwidth, the output edge faithfully tracks the reference's slow phase wander (that is the DLL's whole job: hand the reference through to the output "completely intact", just with a fixed delay added); high-pass, 1−HDLL(s)=s/(s+ωDLL)1-H_{DLL}(s)=s/(s+\omega_{DLL})1−HDLL​(s)=s/(s+ωDLL​), for the delay line's own noise/drift — the loop measures and corrects low-frequency delay-line drift (PVT, slow bias variation), so only fast delay-line noise, above the loop bandwidth where the loop cannot react in time, leaks through to the output. But this low-pass/high-pass shaping is a separate matter from Steps 2–3's "is there a 1/f² accumulation at all": even with HDLLH_{DLL}HDLL​ removed entirely (open loop), Steps 2–3's σref2+Nσstage2\sigma_{ref}^2+N\sigma_{stage}^2σref2​+Nσstage2​ is still bounded, still does not accumulate over time — the loop only decides "which frequency band of the delay line's noise leaks through"; it does not create a κΔt\kappa\sqrt{\Delta t}κΔt​ term, because the delay line was never an integrator to begin with. This is a sharp contrast with the PLL's highpass ∣Hhp∣2\lvert H_{hp}\rvert^2∣Hhp​∣2 (Rule 3): the PLL's highpass exists to cut off the VCO's naturally-divergent 1/f21/f^21/f2 tail; the DLL's highpass merely decides how much of the delay line's already-bounded noise gets through — there is nothing divergent to cut off, because the delay line never diverges. Relation to cdr_bang_bang_jtol: that page's sidebar "why a DLL does not accumulate jitter" describes the leanest possible PI-CDR — the phase code is driven directly by a digital accumulator, with none of this section's analog loop filter, so it does not even do "low-pass the reference noise"; the jitter is inherited from the reference clock directly (see that page's Step 3). What this section adds, HDLL(s)H_{DLL}(s)HDLL​(s), is the extra filtering layer a full analog DLL (such as Maneatis 1996) provides. The core conclusion, "no 1/f² accumulation", is identical on both pages — a full DLL simply adds a tunable filter bandwidth on top. Worked (4-stage delay line vs. Rule 4's buffer floor): import numpy as np N, sigma_stage = 4, 50e-15 sigma_dll = np.sqrt(N) * sigma_stage print(round(sigma_dll * 1e15, 1)) # -> 100.0 N=4N=4N=4, σstage=50\sigma_{stage}=50σstage​=50 fs (illustrative) ⇒σt,DLL=4×50=100.0\Rightarrow\sigma_{t,DLL}=\sqrt4\times50=100.0⇒σt,DLL​=4​×50=100.0 fs — this is an additive, time-independent number from a single pass, and it sits at the same order of magnitude, same category, as Rule 4's Step-5 buffer floor of 16.016.016.0 fs (:262, the same "additive, non-accumulating" physics, just Rule 4 is one buffer stage and this is four delay-line stages): both are power-added and bounded, and can be combined with Rule 4's Step-4 "dB-addition table" directly. Compare against the free-running VCO's random walk (same site-canonical κ2=0.125 rad2/s\kappa^2=0.125\ \text{rad}^2/\text{s}κ2=0.125 rad2/s, [P2] Eq.(8)/(12), p.792–793): import numpy as np kappa2, f0 = 0.125, 5e9 for dt in (1e-6, 1e-3): sigma_phi = np.sqrt(kappa2 * dt) sigma_t = sigma_phi / (2*np.pi*f0) print(dt, round(sigma_t * 1e15, 1)) # -> 1e-06 11.3 # -> 0.001 355.9 The free-running VCO is only 11.311.311.3 fs at Δt=1 μs\Delta t=1\ \mu\text{s}Δt=1 μs (smaller than the DLL's additive 100100100 fs!), but by Δt=1\Delta t=1Δt=1 ms it has already grown to 355.9355.9355.9 fs — because σΔt∝Δt\sigma_{\Delta t}\propto\sqrt{\Delta t}σΔt​∝Δt​ has no upper bound, and the number grows with the measurement window; the DLL's 100100100 fs is the same number no matter how long Δt\Delta tΔt is. This is exactly the design message Rule 5 is meant to deliver: DLL/delay-line-based clock distribution has an inherent advantage over long timescales, at the cost that it cannot do frequency synthesis the way a PLL can (it can only delay, not multiply), and its lock range is limited to one reference period. Step 5 (phase-interpolator quantization: a different kind of "bounded" — deterministic DJ, not random RJ). A DLL produces NNN discrete phase taps (spaced Tref/NT_{ref}/NTref​/N apart). To interpolate a finer phase between taps (for example, a CDR's sampling phase, or a higher-resolution output clock), the standard approach is a phase interpolator (PI): use bbb bits to slice the interval between two adjacent taps (treated as one UI wide) into 2b2^b2b grid points, and the sampled/output phase can only land on a grid point: ΔPI=UI2b[s]\Delta_{PI}=\frac{UI}{2^{b}}\qquad[\text{s}]ΔPI​=2bUI​[s] This is a quantization error, not noise — the same code gives the same delay every time, it is deterministic and bounded (off by at most ±ΔPI/2\pm\Delta_{PI}/2±ΔPI​/2), and it is uniformly distributed (sweep across all possible target phases and the landing error is equally likely anywhere in ±ΔPI/2\pm\Delta_{PI}/2±ΔPI​/2). In this site's DJ language (see dj_dual_dirac's Step-2 DJ classification table): PI quantization is a DJ accounted for by peak-to-peak, and it does not scale with Q−1(BER)Q^{-1}(\text{BER})Q−1(BER): DJpp,PI=ΔPI=UI2b \boxed{\ \mathrm{DJ}_{pp,PI}=\Delta_{PI}=\frac{UI}{2^{b}}\ } DJpp,PI​=ΔPI​=2bUI​ ​ Worked (UI=40UI=40UI=40 ps, 6-bit PI): UI, b = 40e-12, 6 step = UI / 2**b print(round(step * 1e12, 3)) # -> 0.625 print(round(step / UI, 4)) # -> 0.0156 A 6-bit PI slices a 404040 ps UI into 646464 steps, one step =0.625=0.625=0.625 ps ≈0.0156 UI\approx0.0156\ UI≈0.0156 UI (about 0.016 UI0.016\ UI0.016 UI). Dimension check: [s]/[−]=[s][\text{s}]/[-]=[\text{s}][s]/[−]=[s] ✓. Design implication: one more bit of resolution halves the quantization DJ (2b+12^{b+1}2b+1 grid points), but the PI circuit's own differential nonlinearity (DNL) and linearity eat into some of that theoretical resolution — UI/2bUI/2^bUI/2b is a lower bound, not the actual number; a real PI's DJ is usually larger. This row has been added, in sync, to dj_dual_dirac's DJ source table. Failure conditions (specific to Rule 5): (1) a DLL's lock range is only one reference period — the input edge position must fall within the delay line's tunable range, or it will lose lock; this is the fundamental reason a DLL cannot do integer multiplication the way a PLL can; (2) Steps 2–3's "bounded, non-accumulating" result assumes every reference edge makes one independent pass through the delay line — if the same batch of delay-line taps is wired into a ring (taps connected head-to-tail to self-oscillate), it turns back into an oscillator and regains κΔt\kappa\sqrt{\Delta t}κΔt​ accumulation; Rule 5's "no accumulation" no longer holds; (3) PI quantization's uniform-distribution assumption requires the target phase to be distributed arbitrarily across grid points (e.g. a clock-phase sweep/calibration); if the target phase is locked steady near a handful of codes, the actual DJ statistics will deviate from the ideal uniform distribution.
documents.s: Rule 5: DLL — no oscillator, no random walk

documents.t: Put the conclusions of Rules 1 and 2 side by side: ×N gives ϕ×N\phi\times Nϕ×N while the carrier gets f0×Nf_0\times Nf0​×N; ÷N gives ϕ/N\phi/Nϕ/N while f0/Nf_0/Nf0​/N. Substituting into Δt=ϕ/(2πf0)\Delta t=\phi/(2\pi f_0)Δt=ϕ/(2πf0​) (canonical formula 17), the two NNN's cancel: σt,out=σϕ,out2πf0,out=N±1 σϕ,in2π N±1f0,in=σt,in\sigma_{t,out}=\frac{\sigma_{\phi,out}}{2\pi f_{0,out}} =\frac{N^{\pm1}\,\sigma_{\phi,in}}{2\pi\,N^{\pm1} f_{0,in}}=\sigma_{t,in}σt,out​=2πf0,out​σϕ,out​​=2πN±1f0,in​N±1σϕ,in​​=σt,in​ Time jitter in seconds is the invariant of ideal multiplication/division. The L\mathcal{L}L that got worse (or better) is only a change in the exchange rate "the same error in seconds converted to angle". This gives you an extremely useful sanity check: on any chain segment that is "pure ×N/÷N with no additive floor", the σt\sigma_tσt​ computed at both ends over the same integration band must be equal. Verify with the worked chain's numbers (the 5 GHz stage vs the 2.5 GHz after ideal ÷2, both without the buffer): import numpy as np from simulations.common.noise_utils import integrate_rms_jitter f = np.logspace(4, 8, 20001) L5G = np.where(f <= 1e6, -126.02, -148.0 - 20*np.log10(f/1e6)) st5, _ = integrate_rms_jitter(f, L5G, f0=5e9, fmin=1e4, fmax=1e8) st25, _ = integrate_rms_jitter(f, L5G - 6.02, f0=2.5e9, fmin=1e4, fmax=1e8) print(round(st5*1e15, 1)) # -> 22.5 print(round(st25*1e15, 1)) # -> 22.5 The two 22.5 fs values are identical — ÷2 improved L\mathcal{L}L by 6 dB yet saved not a single fs. For SerDes this is actually the flip side of bad news: converted to UI, σt\sigma_tσt​ is unchanged while the UI gets longer, so after division the "fraction of a UI" does shrink — what you save is a ratio, not seconds.
documents.s: Step 5: the conserved quantity — under ideal ×N/÷N, σt\sigma_tσt​ (seconds) is unchanged

documents.t: Now string the four rules into a realistically shaped chain. All values are representative/illustrative (not a specific silicon process) but fully consistent with the site's canonical numbers. Output buffer: Rule 4, power-add against the −155-155−155 floor: 100 kHz: signal −132.04-132.04−132.04 is 22.96 dB above the floor ⇒ penalty ≈0.02\approx0.02≈0.02 dB ⇒ −132.02-132.02−132.02 (floor invisible). 10 MHz: signal −174.02-174.02−174.02 is 19 dB below the floor ⇒ floor dominates ⇒ −154.95-154.95−154.95 (clamped near −155-155−155). Node Carrier L\mathcal{L}L(100 kHz) [dBc/Hz] L\mathcal{L}L(10 MHz) [dBc/Hz] Dominant rule Reference 100 MHz −160.00-160.00−160.00 −160.00-160.00−160.00 — PLL ×50 output 5 GHz −126.02-126.02−126.02 −168.00-168.00−168.00 Rule 3 (in-band ref+34; out-of-band VCO) After ÷2 2.5 GHz −132.04-132.04−132.04 −174.02-174.02−174.02 Rule 2 (−6.02-6.02−6.02) + buffer (final) 2.5 GHz −132.02-132.02−132.02 −154.95-154.95−154.95 Rule 4 (floor dominates at 10 MHz) The same table pinned down with checkable Python: import numpy as np L_ref = -160.0 L_in = L_ref + 20*np.log10(50) # Rule 1/3: in-band = ref + 20logN print(round(L_in, 2)) # -> -126.02 L_vco_10M = -148.0 - 20*np.log10(10e6/1e6) # VCO 1/f²: extrapolate from the 1 MHz anchor to 10 MHz print(round(L_vco_10M, 2)) # -> -168.0 div = -20*np.log10(2) # Rule 2 print(round(L_in + div, 2)) # -> -132.04 print(round(L_vco_10M + div, 2)) # -> -174.02 def padd(*Ls): return 10*np.log10(sum(10**(L/10) for L in Ls)) print(round(padd(L_in + div, -155.0), 2)) # -> -132.02 print(round(padd(L_vco_10M + div, -155.0), 2)) # -> -154.95
